projects.name: Cryogenic Air Separation Digital Twin
projects.tagline: Dynamic air separation twin joining physics, controls, economics, logistics and agentic operations
projects.what: A dynamic, first-principles digital twin of a cryogenic air separation unit, the plant that compresses, purifies, cools and distils air into oxygen, nitrogen and argon. The physics kernel models the main air compressor, molecular-sieve purification, main heat exchanger, turboexpanders, a double distillation column with a crude argon column, storage tanks, an ISA-tagged instrument registry, twelve PID loops with an interlock matrix, an 18-state startup sequencer and a rolling-horizon LP-MPC. Around it sit a historian, a truck-and-hub distribution network, a React control room, multi-agent operations tooling on local LLMs and a generated knowledge base, evolved across a family of related code lines from a desktop prototype through successive simulator rewrites to an agentic microservice variant.
projects.solves: An air separation unit is one of the most electricity-intensive continuous processes in heavy industry, and its economics hinge on tightly coupled constraints: a narrow condenser-reboiler temperature approach, argon recovery that takes hours to re-stabilise after a column upset, compressor surge margin and cryogenic tank boil-off. Operators, process engineers and planners need a safe sandbox for training, a solver for load and dispatch trade-offs usually decided in spreadsheets and email, per-order loss attribution, and fast root-cause analysis after an upset. The twin puts physics, controls, economics, logistics and optimisation on one authoritative plant state.

versus.incumbents: Commercial dynamic process simulators, plant historians, advanced-control suites, spreadsheets and email
versus.edge: Unlike a stack of separate tools, every equation here is readable Python with a fidelity tag, and one process boundary (physics kernel, REST and WebSocket service, browser) carries a historian, economics, logistics and an agent layer together. The rigorous column solver runs in 6.4 ms median warm-started and the LP-MPC in 4.7 ms median. Thermodynamics combine CoolProp with correlations fitted for N2, O2 and Ar at 70 to 120 K.

moves: Desktop monolith to layered web twin: Rebuilt an early PyQt6 prototype, a single 1,675-line file, as a layered web twin that can be shared, embedded and scripted. The rewrite fixed a layer contract that every later iteration kept: physics knows nothing about the UI, controls run as a separate pass, economics is read-only and post-hoc, the historian is append-only and the API is the single gateway.

Focus on one verifiable plant: One rebuild narrowed the multi-plant fleet to a single real plant so every behaviour could be verified end to end. The same step made fault injections write real state, put agent writes (set load, dispatch, maintenance) behind human approval, and moved LLM calls off the physics loop into a throttled queue capped at 3 concurrent calls; the fleet returned later on the hardened base.

Physics rebuild: Replaced an 8-stage argon model with a Fenske-Underwood-Gilliland shortcut sized from a structured-packing height, because a relative volatility of 1.02-1.05 calls for well over 100 trays at high purity. Condenser and reboiler now share one duty, consistent with the First Law, and a plant-wide mass and energy balance auditor was added.

Rigorous solvers with labelled fallbacks: A Wang-Henke MESH solver for the high-pressure, low-pressure and crude argon columns replaced reduced-order lag models, with condenser coupling iterated to a tight tolerance. A rolling-horizon LP on HiGHS replaced the rule-based load heuristic; both earlier methods are retained as fallbacks and every result is tagged with the solver used.

Audit-driven hardening: A code audit logged 421 findings (3 P0, 104 P1, 201 P2, 113 P3), and 94 of 96 P0/P1 findings were confirmed under adversarial verification. The fixes covered the control layer's 12 outputs, eight interlocks and the operator load command, and the test suite grew from 91 to 454 passing tests.

subs.name: Agentic Production-Logistics Command Center
subs.what: A polyglot set of fourteen cooperating services for production-and-logistics decision support: a Next.js control room and a Chainlit workspace in front of a LangGraph three-agent supervisor that calls nine MCP tool servers, a canonical state service and an audit service, with local LLMs on Ollama. Built just before the physics-simulator line, it runs as a complete 16,551-line system with deterministic seeded data adapters.
subs.solves: Production decisions run on process time and distribution decisions on transport time, so a demand collapse is typically handled by phone and spreadsheet with no record of who decided what on what evidence. This gives every disturbance a decision case with evidence and an approver.
subs.edge: Unlike a historian or a supply-chain planning suite, it adds a persisted decision case with evidence references and an approval record. Telemetry stays on-premise because the reasoning runs on local models.
moves: Autonomy policy as data: Five levels (L0 observe up to L4 auto-execute non-safety logistics) are a reviewable table, plus a nine-item never-list (DCS and PLC writes, interlock bypass, purity setpoint override and others) that no level can override.
Domain-first build: The shared domain package was written before the services and is type-checked in CI, so fourteen independently deployable services share one wire format.

subs.name: Shared Domain Model Library
subs.what: A Pydantic library that defines every entity, event and enumeration of the decision-support platform (20 entity classes, 17 event contracts, 12 enumerations), installed as an editable dependency into all fourteen services.
subs.solves: It prevents silent contract drift between services, where a renamed field leaves a panel quietly empty, and gives LLM agents a schema to fill instead of a blank page.
subs.edge: Unlike generated OpenAPI clients, Protocol Buffers or untyped dicts, one artefact delivers runtime validation, JSON Schema for LLM structured output and static types together. Every service imports the same definitions, so the contract is defined once.
moves: Provenance as types: Telemetry values carry quality and provenance, and every network snapshot and agent input carries a state version id, so a decision case cites exactly what it reasoned over and a replay is reproducible.
String enums by design: String enums throughout make comparisons robust and close off the enum-comparison pitfall seen in the simulator line's dispatch path.

subs.name: Multi-Agent Supervisor Service
subs.what: A FastAPI service that owns a compiled LangGraph state machine running a demand and anomaly agent, a plant operations-impact agent and a logistics optimisation agent on each disturbance. Each agent gathers evidence from MCP tools, reasons with a local Ollama model and returns a typed output; the graph pauses at a human approval checkpoint and streams progress to both front ends.
subs.solves: A single big-prompt assistant hallucinates plant constraints, produces prose nobody can audit and either does nothing or everything. This gives each agent a bounded remit, cited evidence and a policy line between recommend and execute.
subs.edge: Unlike a single ReAct agent, chat-driven agent teams or a workflow engine, control flow is an explicit graph of 8 nodes and 4 conditional routers with approval interrupts that checkpoint state. Every step is inspectable, and the policy boundary between recommending and executing is part of the graph itself.
moves: Approval as an interrupt: A LangGraph interrupt before the approval node checkpoints state, so a case can wait hours for a human and resume without re-running the agents.

Constraints from the plant, not the model: Cheap cases short-circuit past later agents, and the operations agent reads ramp rates and minimum loads from the plant tool rather than recalling them, so infeasible scenarios are reported as infeasible.

subs.name: Domain-Bounded MCP Tool Servers
subs.what: Nine small FastAPI services, one per domain (plant, demand, fleet, routing, weather, disruption, simulation, optimisation, governance), exposing 37 tools and 3 resources to the agents. Each has its own settings prefix and an adapter switch between a deterministic seeded data adapter and a source-system adapter.
subs.solves: It lets the reasoning layer be developed and demonstrated independently of enterprise integrations, and avoids a monolithic API where the component that reads telemetry could also approve actions.
subs.edge: Unlike a monolithic API or direct historian access, a semantic tool surface hides the source system and confines each service to one domain. Agents see operations vocabulary rather than tags and tables, and each tool server holds a single, narrow permission set.
moves: Semantic tools over data access: Tool names use the operations vocabulary (feasible operating window, customer coverage), so swapping the plant adapter needs no agent changes.

Deterministic seeded results: Results are seeded on the entity id (plus the current hour where values drift), so demos are reproducible and a different answer on retry signals a real bug; every response also carries a summary and a confidence value.

subs.name: Canonical Network State Service
subs.what: A FastAPI service that holds the canonical state (plants, customers, fleet, routes) of a multi-plant, truck-fleet gas distribution network. It regenerates the state every 15 seconds, keeps a bounded per-plant time series, computes network KPIs and notifies browsers over a WebSocket.
subs.solves: It stops agents and UI panels from forming their own views of the network, so every consumer cites one identified snapshot.
subs.edge: Unlike a tag-oriented historian, per-service state or a shared database, it offers an entity-oriented, version-stamped state with push notification. Every consumer reads the same snapshot, and each decision can point to the exact state it used.
moves: Version-stamped snapshots: Each regeneration gets a new state version id that decision cases cite, which makes the audit trail reconstructable.

Notification plus fetch: The WebSocket sends a small change notice and clients fetch once, keeping the socket cheap. KPIs such as on-time-in-full delivery, fleet utilisation and specific power per tonne of oxygen are computed once, centrally.

subs.name: Streaming Operator Chat Workspace
subs.what: A Chainlit chat application where an operator opens a decision case, watches the three agents' reasoning stream live, sees evidence panels and approves or rejects, which resumes the paused LangGraph run. Conversation history persists in SQLite per browser session.
subs.solves: A dashboard suits state but not reasoning; operators need to watch, question and then approve with a reason, and keep the thread across shifts.
subs.edge: Unlike a chat panel inside the React app, a generic LLM chat or a team messaging tool, every message binds to a decision case, approvals resume the real workflow and nothing leaves the network. The conversation is the control surface for the case.
moves: One stream, two consumers: The workspace reads the same server-sent-event stream as the React UI, so the orchestration service stays the single owner of execution.
Resilient history: A 5-column SQLite table is read newest-first with a limit and reversed for display, and every access is wrapped so the workspace stays available whatever the state of storage.

subs.name: Full-Stack Plant Simulator
subs.what: The mature, continuously operated iteration of the twin: a 53,232-line Python platform that runs one cryogenic plant or a multi-plant fleet in dynamic or accelerated time behind 151 FastAPI endpoints, with a Vite/React control room, a DuckDB and PostgreSQL historian, ten LLM-backed operations agents, a 13-agent root-cause pipeline on local Ollama models and an LP-based load optimiser. It ships as a single docker compose stack.
subs.solves: It answers questions that cross plant physics, economics and distribution at once, such as how a hot day propagates from compressor suction density to purity and argon recovery, and it attributes losses across seven stages from production to invoice.
subs.edge: Unlike commercial dynamic process simulators, it adds economics, logistics, 102 injectable fault scenarios and agents behind a REST API. Thermodynamics use CoolProp plus fitted correlations.
moves: Audit-driven control hardening: A code audit's top findings were fixed across the control layer: controller outputs now survive the state merge, all eight interlocks can trip, and the operator load command carries the requested value. The high-pressure column component-balance error fell from double-digit percent to under 0.1 percent.

Upgrades with labelled fallbacks: A Wang-Henke MESH column solver (6.4 ms median), an LP-MPC on HiGHS (4.7 ms median) and a forecasting layer gated by walk-forward backtesting against a naive baseline replaced simpler versions, each kept as a labelled fallback.

subs.name: Generated Engineering Knowledge Base
subs.what: Three knowledge layers for the simulator: a hand-written engineering canon with a 104-page wiki, a generated link-graph vault of 101 live notes plus 1,935 snapshot files built from the running simulator, historian and root-cause database, and a static site that renders the vault.
subs.solves: It preserves institutional memory alongside the source tree, captures what a simulation run actually did before the bounded in-memory event bus rolls over, and gives new engineers a living reference to how the project is built.
subs.edge: Unlike wiki platforms or autodoc tools, it detects stale pages mechanically from source hashes and links incidents to equipment, alarms and agents. Notes are generated from the running system, so the knowledge base follows the code.
moves: Mechanical staleness: A sha256-plus-mtime map links each source file to the pages that cite it and back, so a changed file marks pages stale automatically and readers see a warning banner until the page is patched.

Snapshots that capture the API surface: Each snapshot freezes the vault, a hash manifest of sources and a set of read-only API responses, so it reproduces what the UI would have shown; snapshot history is preserved across rebuilds.

subs.name: Single-Plant Simulator Rebuild
subs.what: The pivot point of the lineage: a complete single-plant simulator (101 Python modules, 26,043 lines, a 4,750-line browser UI) that focused a multi-plant fleet on one real plant, made fault injections change real state, put an approval gate on agent writes and moved LLM calls off the physics loop.
subs.solves: Verifying behaviour across a multi-plant fleet is slow, fault injections need to change real plant state rather than labels, and LLM calls must never be able to stall the physics loop. This rebuild delivers all three on one verifiable plant.
subs.edge: Unlike fixing the fleet in place or rewriting from scratch, it kept the deterministic kernel and rebuilt the rest against one verifiable case. That gave a clean base for the next round of physics upgrades.
moves: Decision record before code: A written reuse, refactor or replace verdict with line counts for every module, ten modules marked Preserve and eight falsifiable acceptance tests, for example that physics continues during LLM queue saturation and that the queue never exceeds three concurrent calls.

Injections with real physics: Faults write real state such as ambient temperature, an override flag stops the weather engine undoing them, a per-type cleanup reverses effects on expiry, and each active fault maps to an optimiser constraint (an equipment trip becomes a hard load bound of 0, extreme weather a reduced thermal limit).

subs.name: Single-File Control Room UI
subs.what: Nineteen dated iterations of the control-room front end, built as one hand-written HTML file that grew from 8,224 to 10,583 lines with eleven tabs, a hand-drawn SVG process diagram, a three.js plant, 34 canvases, 79 REST endpoints and one WebSocket.
subs.solves: An operator needs live production and economics, customer days-of-inventory ranked by risk, agent decisions with reasoning, optimiser moves and a fault injector on one screen, and a single file removed every barrier to iterating on that.
subs.edge: Unlike licensed HMI suites or Grafana, it shows plant-specific panels such as loss accountability, argon recovery and agent value attribution. Once the file reached 10,583 lines, the line graduated to a Vite/React module build.
moves: Migration to a module build: Moving from the single inline-script file to Vite/React gave the front end structured modules in place of a monolith that would need tests bolted on, with the original kept as a legacy file.

Render and polling discipline: The WebSocket handler only writes shared state while a separate tick renders, and polling loops run only for the visible tab; the React successor computes a LIVE, STALE (over 10 s) or OFFLINE (over 30 s) badge from real poll health.

subs.name: Closed-Loop Planning Simulator Extension
subs.what: A later revision of the full-stack simulator that adds a 7,896-line sales-and-operations planning and execution package (an expanded revival of a smaller layer removed earlier), a genuinely multi-plant backend, new front-end screens and a one-switch LLM provider layer across local and hosted providers. It closes the loop from a market or plant shock through re-forecast, MPC re-solve, financial projection and execution response.
subs.solves: After a market or plant shock, a team needs a revised plan, an approval step and a priced impact, not only a view of what the plant is doing and costing. This revision also makes a multi-plant fleet operating reality, with agents and cascades working on every plant.
subs.edge: Unlike commercial integrated-business-planning suites or a spreadsheet planning cycle, the plan is re-solved against the running twin on every shock. Impact is priced in event-duration dollars, so a planner sees the cost of the actual event.
moves: Signed margin as correctness: Injections are split into favourable and adverse families so an adverse shock must show margin pressure and a demand drop must not book a loss, guarded by a regression test; headline impact now shows event-duration dollars, with annualised figures labelled as 'if sustained'.

Multi-plant hardening: Registered agents dynamically per plant in place of a hardcoded seed, so every plant's agents carry tool permissions, and extended the cascade filter to events targeting trucks, drivers or out-of-set customers.

subs.name: Persian-Language Safety Retrieval Assistant
subs.what: A Persian-language Gradio assistant for air separation plant personnel that answers health, safety and environment questions strictly from a corpus of root-cause-analysis and safety-method documents and cites the exact line range of each source. It also generates a seven-section Permit-To-Work sheet, has an emergency panel for four cryogenic hazards and exports right-to-left PDF.
subs.solves: Safety knowledge sits in long reports nobody reads under time pressure, and a general chatbot that invents a control measure is itself a hazard.
subs.edge: Unlike a PDF shared drive, a general LLM or enterprise EHS platforms, it answers only from the corpus using hybrid retrieval, cites the exact line range of each source and replies 'I don't know' when the corpus gives no support. Answers in Persian stay grounded in the source documents.
moves: Cross-lingual hybrid retrieval: A multilingual 384-dimension embedding model handles Persian questions over an English corpus, and dense search is fused with BM25 at 0.7 and 0.3 with k=25 because incident reports are full of exact identifiers that dense retrieval matches poorly.

Chunking for citations: 500-character chunks keep character and line offsets so a cited span can be highlighted in context; a sibling retrieval pipeline for incident reports uses wider chunks, raised from 900 to 2,200 characters to keep each report coherent.

subs.name: Public-Signal Lead Detection Pipeline
subs.what: A business-development intelligence pipeline that watches about 260 public data sources (SEC filings, EPA air permits, federal awards, county building permits, labour statistics, energy dockets, patents, news) for signs that a company will build, expand or close an industrial facility. It resolves signals to companies and facilities, scores them with a documented model and writes qualified opportunities into Salesforce with an assigned owner; the codebase is 361,659 lines of Python with 92 database migrations and 33 architecture decision records.
subs.solves: Industrial projects take shape long before they are announced, but the public signals that one exists are scattered across hundreds of portals and are mostly noise, so interested parties hear about them late. This pipeline turns that scatter into scored, owned opportunities.
subs.edge: Unlike contact-data vendors, CRM-native lead scoring or commercial project-intelligence databases, it creates leads from permit and regulatory signals using open data and a factor-decomposed score whose weights self-calibrate. Every score decomposes into its contributing factors.
moves: Deterministic, auditable scoring: Base confidence is a weighted sum of source credibility, entity-resolution confidence, specificity, recency and corroboration, with recency half-lives that vary by source type and corroboration counted as distinct evidence hosts in a property-graph walk. No LLM sits on this path, so the number that sends a lead onward is reproducible.

Transactional outbox to the CRM: Opportunity writes use canonical-JSON idempotency keys, batch draining that skips locked rows, exponential backoff and dead-lettering after five attempts, with a database trigger making the payload immutable once written. Extraction passes a four-critic council with a recorded dissent log before arbitration.

subs.name: Industrial Plant Image Generator
subs.what: A small Hugging Face Gradio Space that runs a distilled open text-to-image diffusion model to render photorealistic industrial plants (air separation, LNG, hydrogen, refinery) from seven built-in prompts. It is a standalone image tool for documentation and interface work.
subs.solves: Documentation, decks and interface mockups need specific plant imagery without stock-photo mismatch or the confidentiality issues of real-site photos.
subs.edge: Unlike stock photos, real-site photos or hosted image APIs, it produces an on-brief image in 8 inference steps with seed control and no site attached. Built-in prompts cover air separation, LNG, hydrogen and refinery plants.
moves: Distilled-model settings: Guidance scale is 0.0 with 8 steps by default, because a distilled model has guidance baked in and classifier-free guidance on top would degrade output and double cost.

Dependency isolation: The diffusers and torch stack runs in its own environment, independent of the pinned versions of a sibling assistant project, and a no-op shim lets the same code run outside the Space.

projects.name: Air Separation Digital Twin
projects.tagline: Desktop digital twin for testing air separation setpoints, delivered cost and logistics at zero process risk.
projects.what: A self-contained digital twin and operations trainer for cryogenic air separation units, delivered as a desktop application. It simulates independent plants side by side, each with a physics-constrained reduced-order model, a process tag bus, an economics ledger and a truck and rail loading yard, behind a PyQt6 operator interface with seven views. It is frozen into a single Windows executable of about 68 MB that runs fully offline with no Python installed.
projects.solves: An air separation unit earns or loses margin on a few setpoints (compressor inlet guide vanes, reflux, argon draw, load) traded against purity, CO2 slip, column pressure drop and surge limits. Nobody can safely experiment on a live plant, so operators hold conservative commissioning setpoints and the margin left on the table stays unmeasured. Control-room displays also hide delivered cost per kilogram, and new engineers learn trip causes by causing trips.

versus.incumbents: Rigorous process simulators, advanced process control and real-time optimization suites, plant historians, spreadsheets
versus.edge: Unlike rigorous simulators, which are licensed per seat, need specialists and know nothing about tanks, trucks or delivered cost, this twin joins thermodynamics, a per-product delivered-cost ledger and logistics in one object graph. Where advanced process control acts on the live plant and needs disruptive step tests, the optimizer here scores candidate setpoints on cloned plant states, so experiments carry no process risk.

moves: Three solver generations: The first built the plant as a CasADi/IPOPT nonlinear program (19 variables, 15 equality constraints). The second moved to closed-form correlations that always converge, and the current build uses a physics-constrained model with Fenske minimum-stage feasibility and an enthalpy balance that must close.

Interface-preserving swaps: The solver class name, call signature and returned keys were held constant, so a 575-byte adapter let the 767-line plant kernel absorb a complete physics rewrite with zero edits.

Controlled optimizer experiment: Two builds differ by exactly four changes (two kernel methods, an optimizer module, a UI module, one import) with twelve modules byte-identical, and each is frozen into its own executable. Any difference between them is therefore attributable to the optimizer alone.

Annealing instead of SLSQP: Finite-difference gradients on a stochastic simulation are dominated by noise, so the optimizer uses Metropolis annealing over 40-second multi-plant rollouts with graduated penalties. It runs one iteration per UI frame (about 25 iterations per second), so the operator watches the search converge.

Hardened the physics solver: A damped fixed-point solver with six-level backtracking gained adaptive relaxation (step shrinks 30 % on oscillation, regrows 5 % when stable), and the accepted merit is now kept current at every step so convergence stays reliable.
proof: One-file Windows executable of about 68 MB
27-dimensional observation space for the PPO agent

subs.name: Equation-Oriented Solver Prototype
subs.what: A PyQt6 simulator of independent air separation plants built as an equation-oriented model, with 15 nonlinear equality constraints over 19 decision variables solved by IPOPT through CasADi. It adds a truck and rail yard, an economics ledger and an animated flow diagram.
subs.solves: It provides a mass-conserving plant model, where no returned operating point can create or destroy mass, running inside a real-time simulator.
subs.edge: More defensible than correlation spreadsheets because conservation is a hard constraint enforced by a nonlinear solver rather than fitted curves.
moves: Surrogate-assisted optimizer: It sampled 250 control vectors, fit a degree-2 ridge regression in closed form, screened 40,000 candidates on the surrogate and re-validated the top 40, so 290 expensive solves covered a 40,000-point search.

Warm-started interior point: Each solve started from the previous solution plus the operator's live settings, and the model carried a staged startup, inlet-filter fouling with clean-in-place and isentropic compressor power.

subs.name: Modular Closed-Form Rewrite
subs.what: A rewrite that replaces the nonlinear program with a closed-form analytic model, splits a 1,172-line monolithic entry point into a widget package and moves simulation onto its own thread. It also serves as the control build for the optimizer experiment.
subs.solves: It makes the simulator fast and maintainable enough to run at up to 100x real time, with interlocks that noise cannot trip.
subs.edge: Closed-form correlations always converge, unlike the equation-oriented predecessor, so the simulator never stalls on a solve and stays responsive at high time compression.
moves: Monolith to package: Extracting eight widget modules cut the entry point from 49,241 to 5,548 bytes, an 89 % reduction, in a single session.

Debounced interlocks and substeps: A trip needs a violation to persist beyond a debounce window that only opens after a startup inhibit period, and time compression is integrated as 0.1 s substeps so a 100x speed stays numerically stable.

subs.name: Annealing Setpoint Optimizer
subs.what: The treatment build of the experiment: the same simulator plus four changes that add a working setpoint optimizer. It forks every plant, simulates each candidate for 40 simulated seconds, scores it against one of six objectives with four toggleable constraints and accepts or rejects by Metropolis annealing, and recommendations stay advisory until an operator applies them.
subs.solves: It searches compressor, reflux, argon and load setpoints for better margin without perturbing a live plant.
subs.edge: Cheaper per iteration than genetic or swarm methods and valid on noisy simulations where SLSQP is not.
moves: Cloned rollouts: Each clone copies controls, tank inventory and the smoothed electricity price but draws a fresh random seed, so a candidate cannot be rewarded for one lucky noise sequence.

Graduated penalties: Penalties grow linearly with violation size and are normalised by each spec, with the trip penalty two orders of magnitude above the rest, so near-feasible candidates keep a slope toward feasibility and no economic gain can buy a trip.

subs.name: Physics-Constrained Model Executable
subs.what: The packaged model: the correlation solver is replaced by a physics-constrained reduced-order model (Fenske minimum stages, relative-volatility surrogates, structured-packing pressure drop and an enthalpy balance that must close), with a rule-based control-system supervisor and a weighted-average-cost inventory ledger from compressor power to customer gate. It is built into a one-file Windows executable of about 68 MB.
subs.solves: It replaces a fitted model that could not explain behaviour, such as why argon recovery drops under stress, and extends costing past the plant fence line.
subs.edge: Unlike licensed simulators, it is wired to a continuously updated profit-and-loss ledger, so every physical change shows up as delivered cost.
moves: Superlinear stage feasibility: The ratio of installed to minimum stages, raised to the power 1.4 and clamped, makes a column short of its minimum stage count stop separating rather than separate slightly worse. Argon, with relative volatility near 1.2, therefore collapses first under stress.

Cost carried into the truck: Tank cost basis updates continuously as production accrues, each vehicle records the blended cost of what it loaded, and delivered cost adds that vehicle's haul cost spread over its capacity.

subs.name: Reinforcement Learning and Failure Modeling
subs.what: The largest build wraps the plant in a Gymnasium environment (27-dimensional observation, 4-dimensional continuous action), adds a dual-mode optimizer that anneals immediately while training a PPO agent on a background thread, and adds a Weibull-hazard equipment-failure model with a timed maintenance state machine. It falls back to annealing automatically if the RL stack is unavailable.
subs.solves: Annealing returns a point, not a policy, and must be re-run as conditions drift, while threshold-only trips teach nothing about operating with margin against random equipment failure.
subs.edge: Unlike linear MPC identified from step tests and steady-state optimization, which do not address transients or failures, this trains a nonlinear policy on a simulator that includes both.
moves: Hot-swap from annealing to PPO: Annealing answers within one UI frame while PPO trains on a daemon thread in 20 chunks, and a lock held only for the handle assignment lets the optimizer switch to inference without blocking the GUI. Both modes are scored by the same rollout and penalty function, so results are comparable.

Weibull failure hazards: Pump cavitation, turbine bearing vibration (accelerated by hot ambient) and a sticky valve each follow their own Weibull shape and characteristic life. The sticky valve is silent, shifting the apparent operating point without an alarm, so detection comes from the process response.

projects.name: Gas Operations Agent Coordination Layer
projects.tagline: Multi-agent layer that reconciles plant, logistics and demand advice into one ranked, human-approved action.
projects.what: A coordination layer for industrial gas operations in which specialised agents for plant process, fleet logistics and demand reason independently, then have conflicting recommendations reconciled into one ranked action with a reason, a confidence number and an estimated financial impact. A human operator approves, defers or rejects it, and the system never writes setpoints. It is built as a runnable service (FastAPI, LangGraph, Ollama, Next.js, Chainlit) alongside a detailed reference-architecture specification.
projects.solves: Plant engineers, dispatchers, reliability teams and energy buyers each optimise locally, so value leaks across the boundaries: a demand spike triggers an external purchase while the plant holds steady load and power is bought at peak. Advanced process control optimises only inside one plant, and operators ignore recommendations they cannot audit, so every recommendation carries a one-sentence reason, a confidence percentage and a net impact estimate.

versus.incumbents: Plant historians, predictive-maintenance tools, separate advanced process control and routing tools, chat assistants
versus.edge: Historians describe, reliability tools watch one asset, and process-control and routing tools work in isolation. This design adds a reconciliation step between a plant optimiser and a logistics optimiser behind a read-only boundary, with local-model inference so telemetry stays on site and a tamper-evident audit log behind every recommendation.

moves: Fixed graph instead of an agent loop: Orchestration is a LangGraph graph of demand analysis, operations analysis, logistics optimisation and a human gate, with no cycles or conditional edges. The steps are causally ordered, and a fixed graph is auditable and bounded in token cost.

Compounding-error budget: The risk analysis works out 85 % per-step accuracy over 10 steps as about 20 % end-to-end success. That reasoning sets a hard cap on workflow depth, with any increase tied to measured per-step reliability.

Specification expansion: An initial outline was extended with cost control for agents that consume far more tokens than a single chat call, an evaluation regime with a sealed held-out set, governance and agent operations, and a write-back design that charts the path from a dashboard of insights to a system that changes the plant.

Local models per role: Inference runs locally through Ollama with a different model for each agent role (Qwen, Gemma, Llama) because plant telemetry should not leave the site; the reference architecture generalises this into a small router model feeding a larger primary model.

Approval surface split by modality: Chainlit owns the approve, defer or reject conversation and Next.js owns the map and KPI views, with Chainlit embedded rather than rebuilt. The frontend was rebuilt as a full project around an earlier prototype page, adding the mapping dependency that page needed.
proof: Fixed four-step orchestration graph with a human approval gate

projects.name: Multi-Model Deliberation Council
projects.tagline: Five different LLMs answer as plant disciplines, rank each other blind, and a chairman synthesises advice.
projects.what: A decision-support service that answers an air separation engineering question by convening five large language models from different families, each cast as a process, rotating-equipment, controls, safety or energy engineer. The experts answer in parallel, three models then rank the anonymised answers, and a reasoning-model chairman synthesises a prioritised recommendation with a confidence level and caveats. Every response carries a decision-support-only disclaimer and a confirmation-required flag that is always true.
projects.solves: Diagnosing an operating plant is multi-disciplinary, and the disciplines read the same symptom differently; in practice their views arrive over hours and the most confident voice tends to win. Asking one model instead gives confident monoculture with no signal about which claims others would dispute, which is worse than visible disagreement for high-stakes advice.

versus.incumbents: Single-model chat, LangChain chains, AutoGen conversations, CrewAI personas, single LLM judges
versus.edge: Stage one runs five concurrent calls so no expert sees another's answer, avoiding the anchoring of sequential chains. Three fixed stages cost exactly 9 model calls, unlike unbounded round-robin conversations, and each role runs on a different model family rather than a persona over one model, so errors are decorrelated and disagreement is visible.

moves: One model to five families: Moved from a single GPT-4o endpoint prompted five ways to five different families (Gemini, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V3) bound to the five disciplines through an aggregator. This decorrelated errors and made peer ranking genuinely independent, with four backend modules rewritten.

Lightweight gateway with compatibility shims: A hand-written async HTTP client over one OpenAI-style wire format replaced vendor SDKs, and retained compatibility shims let the provider change land without touching callers.

Blind peer review: Answers are relabelled Response A to E with the key held server-side, and three reviewers reason first and then emit a strict final-ranking block. It is parsed with three regex fallback tiers and aggregated as mean rank position, keeping the reviewer count so partial rankings stay visible.

Cost and failure handling: Stage two uses three reviewers instead of five, a 40 % cut in review calls. Failed model calls become placeholders so the council keeps five seats, and only total failure returns an error.

Safety cannot be outvoted: A safety-first priority order in the chairman prompt, a safety framework option that emphasises it further, and a keyword escalation over every expert's raw text each surface safety concerns regardless of consensus.
proof: Exactly 9 model calls: 5 parallel, 3 sequential, 1 final
10.6 KB of hand-written cryogenic domain knowledge in prompts

projects.name: Quantitative Options Trading Platform
projects.tagline: Rust options-trading platform with bit-identical replay, a fail-closed risk governor and a full audit log.
projects.what: A from-scratch quantitative trading platform that runs entirely on one laptop. A Rust modular monolith ingests market data, computes features, generates option-structure candidates, filters them through a deterministic risk governor, passes approved candidates to a broker adapter built on the broker's native API, records every step in an append-only audit log, and can replay the whole chain with bit-identical results. A Python research environment, a React dashboard, an option scanner and several command-line tools surround it.
projects.solves: Anyone running automated options strategies has no reliable way to know whether a strategy works, because common tools lean toward saying it does: modelled prices shown as fills, look-ahead leakage, selection bias from large parameter sweeps, commission-only cost models, duplicate orders after ambiguous submits, and risk limits that drift. The platform makes those failure modes structurally hard and makes every result falsifiable.

versus.incumbents: Hosted backtesting platforms, NautilusTrader, Backtrader/Zipline, broker APIs, spreadsheets plus a broker web interface
versus.edge: The backtest and execution paths run the same components in the same order, the event log and inputs stay local, and a pinned compiler keeps replay deterministic. Nothing reaches a broker without an approval token that only the risk crate can construct, so the safety boundary is enforced by the type system rather than by convention.

moves: Authority boundary as a compile error: Strategies, models and any LLM adapter can only emit a trade candidate, and the risk governor alone produces the approval type the broker adapter requires by value. Compile-fail tests and a dependency-graph test that fails the build if any proposing crate can reach execution back this up.

Determinism by construction: Reading the OS clock is banned outside one crate by a build-failing test, and the normal CDF and random generator are hand-implemented so a dependency update cannot silently change replay bits. A weighted engine scorecard chose this custom design over NautilusTrader and Barter-rs because the top-weighted criterion was that only Rust code can submit orders.

Broker and daemon migrations: Migrated to a broker's native socket API by implementing the protocol from scratch with two sessions on distinct client identifiers, hardening six edge cases in sequence, such as chains truncated at 1,000 contracts and a one-sided book halving the spot price. Replacing a scheduled one-shot with a resident loop cut a decision from 5,341 ms of cold start plus up to 60 s of scheduler granularity to about 200 ms.

Chain reconstruction: Expired option chains cannot be listed, so they are rebuilt from deterministic contract symbols and a historical-bars endpoint, where a miss proves the contract never existed. Results are cached, so a second rebuild of the same date makes no requests.

Statistics that refuse to flatter: Modelled and historical-executable results are different types with no addition between them, and large parameter sweeps are judged with false-discovery correction so only results that survive chance-level expectations count.

subs.name: Offline Research and Forecaster Training
subs.what: The offline Python half of the platform, owning statistical validation (purged cross-validation, deflated Sharpe ratio, probability of backtest overfitting) and training a multi-task Gaussian news forecaster on both PyTorch and JAX, exporting weights the Rust core can load. It is kept separate from the execution path, so research code never touches risk decisions, broker state or orders.
subs.solves: It stops selection bias and look-ahead leakage from turning noise into an apparent edge: over 100 pure-noise paths the best raw annualised Sharpe of 1.06 deflates to 0.3767 and is correctly flagged as not significant.
subs.edge: Unlike plain time-series splitters, which have no purge or embargo, and library implementations that are easy to omit, the gates here apply purging and embargo and return a pass or fail verdict. The export path to the Rust core is tested.
moves: Planted-leak controls: With a signal set equal to the forward return, shuffles and inversion all behaved as expected, and the one-bar signal delay was the control that exposed the leak, retaining 88 % of the fabricated performance.

Leak-proof training: A gain decomposition separates variance-timing gain from directional gain so a volatility model cannot pass as an edge, and integrity checks assert that examples sharing a symbol and session share one label and never straddle a split.

subs.name: Option-Chain Candidate Pipeline
subs.what: The signal-selection subsystem: Rust crates and a daemon narrow thousands of optionable US equities to the few tens whose option chains can be priced within the broker's market-data-line limit, rank them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion over eight server-side screens, and publish the whole funnel, including every rejection with its reason and stage, as an atomic JSON snapshot shown in a dependency-free browser console.
subs.solves: The broker caps concurrent market-data lines and one option chain costs roughly two dozen lines to price, so only on the order of ten names can be priced at once. Line-aware selection prevents starved chains from producing false refusals, and the full-funnel snapshot says exactly why any watched name is missing.
subs.edge: The broker's built-in scanner and vendor screeners rank cheaply and stop there, whereas this uses free wide screens and spends scarce lines on survivors whose chains are fully priced, with every exclusion explained.
moves: Line ledger as a resource lease: A reservation is taken before a request is sent and released only after the cancel has gone out, and a hold dropped without release is counted as abandoned because the broker is still serving that line. Exhaustion is a named error that lists the holders.

Credit-spread ranking key: Spreads are ranked by expectancy per unit of risk, sorted toward the thinnest credit, since every spread risked nearly the same amount. Multiplying by credit as a fraction of max loss, applied only when expectancy is positive, keeps higher-credit spreads from sinking to the bottom of the list.

projects.name: Small-Cap Equity Research Toolkit
projects.tagline: Patent-first research that gates a Monte Carlo of milestones and dilution for small-cap growth companies.
projects.what: A local research toolkit for small and mid-cap growth companies that scores a granted patent estate against the product architecture, then uses that score to gate and tilt a 250,000-path Monte Carlo of milestones, staged dilution and terminal value. The output is a distribution of outcomes paired with a mechanical decision rule. Supporting modules cover a market-wide SEC XBRL screen, a dilution verifier, an industry-relationship graph, an EDGAR early-warning monitor, a reinforcement-learning allocator and a React dashboard fed by static JSON.
projects.solves: Separating a real moat from a press release is hard for pre-revenue and early-revenue companies, and so is pricing the dilution that sits between company outcomes and shareholder outcomes. Raw SEC share counts mislead because splits, listing-year effects and fiscal calendars distort them, and a patent count says nothing about whether the revenue-critical architecture is claimed. The toolkit puts each of these questions on a primary-source footing.

versus.incumbents: Financial data terminals, patent-landscape platforms, spreadsheet scenario tables
versus.edge: Unlike patent platforms that stop at a landscape and terminals that stop at normalized fundamentals, this toolkit links a granted claim to a milestone probability and a dilution ladder inside one model. It restates share counts from primary SEC filings onto today's share basis and labels every dilution figure VERIFIED, SINGLE_SOURCE, DISPUTED or UNAVAILABLE, so each number carries its evidence status.

moves: Template to engine: Generalised a single-company Monte Carlo script into a ticker-parameterised engine with per-company milestone ontologies, YAML priors, a mechanical decision rule and numerical guards.

Screen rebuilt on primary sources: Moved a screening workbook from vendor-derived data to SEC XBRL frames, correcting four issues (non-operating securities in the pool, double-counted share classes, missing exchanges and an endpoint multiple that ignored dilution) and documenting how far each had shifted the share-count figures.

Five-check dilution verifier: Each fiscal year is restated by the cumulative split factor, started after the listing year, scale-checked against market cap divided by price, rate-checked and cross-validated against an independent public price-data series. Close agreement is VERIFIED; disagreement adopts the more conservative value instead of an average.

Dilution decay model: Chose an issuance rate that decays exponentially toward a low long-run level and compounds along the resulting path, rather than holding a young company's current rate flat over a long horizon.

Correlated drivers and reproducibility: Five drivers are drawn through a Cholesky factor so a poor financing market lowers multiples and raises dilution together, milestone probabilities shift in log-odds space, and a fixed seed plus a SHA-256 input checksum stamped into every report make any run reproducible.

subs.name: Patent Moat Scoring Pipeline
subs.what: A staged pipeline that turns unstructured patent-database output into a single auditable 0-100 moat score per company, with a family-level breakdown and element-by-element claim charts. It is the entry gate of the valuation model.
subs.solves: A patent count says little; the useful questions are whether granted claims read on the shipping product, how long the revenue-critical family runs, whether it can block a competitor and where it is enforceable. The pipeline answers each with a scored, documented dimension.
subs.edge: Where commercial patent platforms deliver a landscape for the analyst to interpret, this scores architecture alignment per company and states confidence numerically per family. The reasoning behind each score is written down alongside it.
moves: Weighted composite with a calibration step: Five 0-100 dimensions (claim breadth, architecture alignment, remaining term, blocking power, geographic coverage) roll up per portfolio with explicit weights, then the mechanical score is adjusted for competitive reality, with the reasoning written down.

Assignee resolution and continuation accounting: Name matching alone is unreliable (a search on one financial company returned unrelated agricultural patents), so the pipeline resolves acquired subsidiaries and caps expiry where a terminal disclaimer applies, keeping remaining-term scores accurate.

subs.name: SEC Filing Dilution Verifier
subs.what: A primary-source SEC ingestion layer with three products: a market-wide XBRL screening funnel, a five-check split-adjusted dilution verifier cross-checked against an independent price-data series, and a polling EDGAR monitor for dilution-related filings and insider-sale clusters.
subs.solves: Raw XBRL share counts sit on the share basis in force at filing time, so splits, de-SPAC years and fiscal-year mismatches make naive dilution rates wrong. The verifier restates every figure onto a common basis before any rate is computed.
subs.edge: Where data vendors ship one normalized number with no epistemic status, this shows its split restatement and labels each figure with one of four verification statuses. The monitor runs as a single polling CLI over EDGAR.
moves: Reverse splits as a disqualifier: Large overnight share-count drops are detected, restated to today's base and excluded, treating a reverse split as a record of past holder dilution rather than a buyback.

Base-rate-aware screening: The screen publishes its own prior, comparing how often names reach an extreme outcome over a lifetime versus within a fixed horizon, so every hit is read against the base rate.

subs.name: Patent-Gated Monte Carlo Engine
subs.what: A 250,000-path simulator that turns a patent score, a cap table, a market-size forecast and a YAML prior file into a distribution over a company's terminal value, then applies a mechanical decision rule. Several company-specific milestone trees share one set of plumbing.
subs.solves: For companies with no earnings, DCF and comps degrade into guesses; outcomes depend on a chain of conditional milestones and on how much stock is issued along the way. The engine models both directly.
subs.edge: Spreadsheet scenario tables cannot express conditional milestone chains or correlated financing and dilution, and Monte Carlo add-ins leave the milestone tree and dilution ladder to be built by hand. Here both are first-class, driven by per-company YAML priors.
moves: Log-odds milestone logic: Each milestone probability is logistic(logit(base) plus driver loadings) combined with its parent event, which keeps probabilities inside 0 and 1 without clipping artifacts.
Distressed-branch left tail: Failure is modelled with a moat-scaled distressed branch instead of zero recovery, so deep-tail probabilities stay realistic relative to the mean.

subs.name: Reinforcement-Learning Portfolio Allocator
subs.what: A PPO agent trained with Stable-Baselines3 to allocate weights across a universe of assets plus cash. It is evaluated by expanding-window walk-forward testing against baselines run through the identical environment, with a deflated-Sharpe adjustment on the aggregate.
subs.solves: Allocation across thin microcaps is sequential and cost-sensitive, and most day-to-day variance is common market beta, which swamps any selection signal under an absolute-return reward. Rewarding excess return isolates the part of the decision that reflects selection.
subs.edge: Where open-source RL trading environments pair absolute-return rewards with flat MLP policies, this allocator replaces both with an excess-return reward and a shared per-asset scorer. Baselines run through the identical environment, so every comparison is like for like.
moves: Excess-return reward: Rewarding return relative to the equal-weight return of the valid asset set cancels market beta, so only departures from equal weight earn reward.
Permutation-equivariant policy: Replaced a flat MLP with a shared per-asset scorer that learns what kind of asset deserves weight and can score assets it has never seen.

subs.name: Industry-Relationship Graph
subs.what: A connected-market analysis module beside the valuation core that regresses each stock on the market plus its industry complex. A sufficient lift in explained variance labels a name relationship-driven; otherwise it is market-driven, idiosyncratic or mixed.
subs.solves: Per-company price features cannot see moves caused by a company being a node in someone else's architecture decision. The graph makes those dependencies visible and measurable.
subs.edge: Factor-model attribution tools describe statistical exposure, while this graph is built on declared supply relationships from deep-dive research, with rolling correlation neighbours as a secondary signal.
moves: Explicit edges before learned edges: Relationships taken from deep-dive research are primary, and rolling correlation neighbours, rebuilt causally from a trailing window, exist to catch relationships the research did not name.
Incremental R-squared regimes: Daily returns regress on market plus industry complex; beta-to-complex serves as the amplification measure and the lift in explained variance sets the regime label.

subs.name: Static Research Dashboard
subs.what: An 11-route React single-page application that renders every pipeline stage from a 20-file static JSON contract, with a light and dark design-token system and accessible chart primitives.
subs.solves: The analysis produces long written reports, large path files and many JSON artifacts that are impractical to read as raw files. The dashboard turns them into one navigable view.
subs.edge: Unlike notebook-based dashboards, it needs no running Python process and can be hosted statically anywhere. Changing an assumption is a rerun of the Python pipeline and a rebuild of the JSON contract.
moves: Lenient JSON parsing: Python's json.dump emits bare NaN and Infinity, which are illegal JSON, so the client retries a failed parse with those tokens rewritten to null in value position only, leaving strings untouched.
Missing files as a normal state: Later pipeline stages produce their files afterwards, so a 404 or an HTML fallback response is classified as missing rather than as an error.

projects.name: Portfolio Decision Cockpit
projects.tagline: Self-hosted portfolio cockpit with versioned algorithms, options structures and full decision traces.
projects.what: A containerised, single-operator portfolio-management cockpit and quantitative research platform. It ingests data by CSV, OFX or QFX import, runs two strategy sleeves (long-horizon equity screening and short-dated defined-risk options) through one decision engine that records every decision end to end, and exposes about 36 versioned algorithms behind a governed registry. A Next.js cockpit sits on top.
projects.solves: Decisions are usually kept as outcomes without the reasoning behind them, options-structure selection is manual enumeration, and personal backtests often admit lookahead. The platform persists a trace of every scan, applies a composable constraint and risk pipeline that records an explicit NOOP instead of auto-picking a failed candidate, generates nine canonical options structures and enforces point-in-time data access structurally.

versus.incumbents: Financial data terminals, cloud backtesting platforms, broker trading platforms, web portfolio analyzers
versus.edge: Unlike terminals and broker platforms that show results, this platform adds persisted reasoning for every decision, a VaR family, factor attribution and a governance lifecycle for user-written algorithms. Point-in-time correctness is enforced in the type system rather than left to convention.

moves: Slice-based growth and a single-head guard: Development proceeded as numbered slices, and when one slice forked into three parallel migration branches, CI gained a check that counts Alembic revisions and requires exactly one head.

Point-in-time at the type level: A single DataReader is the only path to data, every read carries an as-of date, and reading a vendor that is not point-in-time correct for a past date raises an error unless an ingest worker explicitly overrides it.

Shadow-mode learned ranker: A pairwise-logistic re-ranker runs in shadow mode, logs the ordering it would have chosen into every decision trace, and needs an explicit governance transition before it can change a decision.

Deterministic execution simulator: Seven mechanisms (spread absorption, an option slippage floor in basis points, volume-participation impact, stale-quote rejection, open-interest partial fills, limit checks and seeded jitter) shape simulated fills, so every run is reproducible.

subs.name: Versioned Algorithm Registry
subs.what: A registry that makes every mathematical kernel a versioned, source-hashed, schema-published object keyed by id and version, benchmarked, parity-checked against an optional native path and mirrored into Postgres. Kernels move through an experimental, candidate, active and deprecated lifecycle in which each transition is gated on stored evidence.
subs.solves: It prevents silent drift when a calculation is edited, version ambiguity between runs, promotion on confidence rather than evidence, and analytics whose inputs and speed the user cannot see.
subs.edge: Where model registries manage trained artifacts with permission-gated staging, this governs pure analytic kernels with evidence-gated promotion. Every promotion is backed by stored tests, benchmarks and research artifacts.
moves: Evidence-gated promotion: Moving a candidate to active requires passing tests, a benchmark run, no benchmark regression, parity or shadow evidence, research artifacts and a walk-forward or bootstrap artifact; failures return a structured list, and success writes a promotion record and audit row in one transaction.

Semver tuple resolution and source hashing: The latest version resolves by a numeric version tuple rather than string order, so a tenth minor release outranks a ninth, and a blake2b hash of each class's source makes silent edits detectable.

subs.name: Options Structure Selection Engine
subs.what: A subsystem that resolves an options chain with provenance, decides which structure families suit the current volatility regime, enumerates candidates across nine structure types, prices payoff and assignment risk, ranks them and routes the winner through the same constraint pipeline and fill simulator as the equity sleeve.
subs.solves: Choosing options structures by hand is a combinatorial problem with a regime dependency. The engine lets the volatility regime decide which families are considered and ranks every candidate on a common footing.
subs.edge: Where broker platforms focus on chain display, this ranks candidates across structure families and persists the rejected ones alongside the winner, with provenance recorded for every Greek.
moves: Regime gate before enumeration: IV rank and term-structure regime decide which structure kinds are allowed, so iron condors in low volatility and calendars in backwardation are never enumerated.

Provenance for every Greek: Where a vendor chain omits Greeks or implied volatility, the registered analytical kernel fills them and the source is recorded, so each candidate carries provenance instead of a null-filled row.

projects.name: Multi-Agent Trading Research Backtester
projects.tagline: Three-agent LangGraph research on a local Ollama model, backtested walk-forward against buy-and-hold.
projects.what: A multi-agent trading research system: a technical analyst, a news sentiment analyst and a decision agent wired into a LangGraph state machine and driven by a local Ollama model. It runs either a one-shot decision on current data or a day-by-day historical walk-forward backtest, through a Click CLI and a Streamlit dashboard.
projects.solves: Walk-forward backtests on hosted frontier models get expensive fast: a 2-year backtest at a 5-day cadence is about 100 decision points with 2-3 LLM calls each. Running on a local model removes the per-call cost, and the backtest tests whether decisions beat holding the stock instead of showcasing one impressive call.

versus.incumbents: Open-source multi-agent trading frameworks, cloud backtesting platforms, open-source backtesting libraries, investing news sites
versus.edge: Unlike larger frameworks that run ten or more agents in debate rounds on hosted models, this uses three isolable agents on a local model, so each signal can be attributed to its source. It reports alpha against buy-and-hold beside Sharpe and drawdown.

moves: JSON mode instead of tool calling: Small local models cannot rely on tool schemas, so every prompt demands one JSON object and the parser strips code fences, extracts the outermost braces and returns a structured parse-error record instead of raising, which degrades a bad response to HOLD.

Direction from the model, size from code: The decision agent only emits BUY, SELL or HOLD, and deterministic backtest code handles sizing and transaction costs, so a hallucinated quantity can never reach the simulation.

Decision cadence as a runtime dial: The agents are consulted every N trading days (default 5) while the equity curve is marked every day, so Sharpe and drawdown stay accurate at a coarse decision cadence.
Lookahead guard for news: yfinance headlines carry no per-date history, so news is switched off in both backtest paths to keep future information out.

Three-level offline degradation: The ticker universe cache refreshes on a 24-hour TTL, a corrupt cache triggers a refetch, a failed refetch falls back to the cache and a missing cache falls back to a curated list, so the UI always renders.

projects.name: Organizational-Memory Lakehouse
projects.tagline: Iceberg and MinIO lakehouse that turns git, folders and session transcripts into searchable knowledge.
projects.what: The system ingests an organization's work from Git repositories, arbitrary folders and local coding-session transcripts into a governed Apache Iceberg lakehouse stored on MinIO. Two silver tables (artifacts and edges) feed five gold marts, a 384-dimensional vector index, a people-files-topics knowledge graph and a grounded question-answering endpoint. DuckDB and Trino read the same tables through one shared catalog, and it ships as a Python package with a CLI, a FastAPI service and a zero-Docker desktop app.
projects.solves: A directory of Parquet files in object storage is not a table: concurrent writers corrupt each other, readers see torn views and yesterday's data is gone. Organizationally, knowledge also lives in uncommitted files and session transcripts that code search never sees, which causes duplicated work and slow onboarding.

versus.incumbents: Managed cloud data warehouses, workflow orchestrators, enterprise search tools, code-search platforms
versus.edge: Everything sits on an open table format in storage the operator owns, with no metered compute and any Iceberg-capable engine able to attach, whereas managed warehouses take custody of the data. Where knowledge tools cover only committed code or SaaS silos, this ingests non-git files and session transcripts into tables the operator owns.

moves: Iceberg from the first commit: The initial commit proved the lakehouse with a smoke test asserting that Parquet and metadata JSON objects physically exist in the bucket, rather than only claiming it.

Catalog migration that moves no data: Promoting the catalog from SQLite to a Postgres JDBC catalog shared with Trino only re-registers metadata pointers, so it takes seconds at any data volume and rolls back by unsetting one environment variable. A standalone smoke test first proved that pyiceberg and Trino read identical rows.

Zero-Docker desktop: The app downloads the official MinIO binary, verifies its published SHA-256 checksum before executing it, supervises it as a child process and adopts an already running instance instead of fighting for the port; the AGPL binary is fetched at runtime and never bundled into the MIT repository.

Deterministic content-derived ids: Ids are a SHA-256 of source, kind and natural key joined with a separator, which makes re-ingestion idempotent without coordination and keeps two different keys from colliding.

Bounded co-edit graph: Files changed together in a commit become weighted edges, and very large commits skip the fan-out, since a single 300-file commit would otherwise create tens of thousands of pairwise edges.
proof: 5 end-to-end tests running against real MinIO, Iceberg and the embedder

subs.name: Lakehouse Field Guide Documentation
subs.what: A LaTeX documentation system beside the code that produces a long, multi-chapter data engineer's field guide and a short technical whitepaper. Both embed real screenshots from a running instance, and the code listings are trimmed extracts from the actual modules.
subs.solves: READMEs explain commands but not why a lakehouse is shaped as it is, and wikis drift from the code; the guide and whitepaper make the concepts and technology choices legible to new engineers and non-implementers.
subs.edge: API reference generators document signatures rather than architecture, while each chapter here follows a four-beat structure (plain idea, data-engineering lens, real code, build-it-yourself box) grounded in a named source module.
moves: Build tooling for encoding and structure: A sanitizer maps dozens of Unicode glyphs to ASCII idempotently, and a checker reports unbalanced listing and environment pairs per chapter before compiling, because one unbalanced begin produces an error hundreds of lines from its cause.
Resilient chapter include: A missing chapter file renders a visible pending marker, so a partial build still compiles.

projects.name: Logistics and Asset Optimization Suite
projects.tagline: Three optimization platforms for bulk delivery routing, catalogue consolidation and returnable-asset capital.
projects.what: A set of three independently runnable platforms for a bulk-product distribution operation: a cryogenic delivery route optimizer built on OR-Tools, a packaged-product SKU consolidation tool built on CP-SAT, and a returnable-asset capital-planning platform driven by five CP-SAT models and a six-agent decision pipeline. Together they carry six distinct mathematical programs, including a hand-written LNS matheuristic for routing.
projects.solves: Bulk liquid delivery is vendor-managed inventory, so daily dispatch combines replenishment and routing under boil-off, product-dedicated trailers, hazmat rules and driver hours. The second problem is capital: deciding which assets to renew, which SKUs to retire and where to move stock is often settled by negotiation rather than optimization.

versus.incumbents: Commercial route-optimization suites, fleet telematics vendors, tank telemetry vendors, ERP systems, spreadsheets and dispatcher whiteboards
versus.edge: Unlike commercial route-optimization suites, these tools make domain constraints such as boil-off and product-dedicated trailers primitives of the model itself. Editable rules are versioned into every run, everything operates offline with data kept on the machine, and every solve is auditable.

moves: Routing first, then two attacks on capital: A routing workbench came first, then SKU consolidation, then asset-lifecycle capital allocation, and finally a benchmarking harness to test the routing strategy against classical and stock OR-Tools baselines on real road distances.

Process isolation by design: Each platform runs as its own single-process service with a self-contained local runner, and the routing platform serves its statically exported UI from the same process, so one command is the entire runtime.

Auditability as a shared principle: The routing platform recomputes its objective by hand after every solve and validates the shipped plan independently, while the capital platform reports solver status, model dimensions and solve time on every response.

Mocks and live adapters for every provider: Seven provider capabilities (routing matrices, weather, traffic, road restrictions, geocoding, fuel price and an LLM narration layer) each have a deterministic mock and a live adapter, so the platforms run fully offline.
proof: 271 tests and 58 REST endpoints in the routing platform
Six mathematical programs across three platforms

subs.name: Cryogenic Route Optimizer
subs.what: A web platform that validates a bulk-liquid delivery history against a canonical data contract and solves daily dispatch as a capacitated, multi-trip, time-constrained vehicle-routing problem per terminal. Dispatchers get a map, an explanation for each stop, a decomposition of where the plan differs from what actually happened and an approvable, exportable plan with a reproducibility snapshot.
subs.solves: Dispatch is a combined replenishment and routing decision in which product boils off in transit, trailers are product-dedicated and payloads are legally capped. Manual dispatching cannot evaluate counterfactuals or audit the plan; this platform does both.
subs.edge: It solves with the same class of model as commercial route-optimization suites (OR-Tools RoutingModel plus a hand-written LNS), owned outright with rules snapshotted into each run. In strict road-true mode it declines to price a group on straight-line distance.
moves: Road-true by default: Migrated routing from great-circle distance with a circuity factor to block-chunked road matrices and then to a self-hosted Valhalla with truck and hazmat costing, where strict mode declines a group instead of estimating.
Vehicle fixed-cost objective: Added a vehicle fixed cost and a shift-packing layer so the solver consolidates work onto fewer trucks instead of spreading it across many lightly used ones.

subs.name: SKU Consolidation Optimizer
subs.what: A fully local web application that takes a packaged-product portfolio extract, classifies each SKU on a popularity-by-price quadrant grid and solves a CP-SAT consolidation model per product family. The model decides which SKUs to keep and where dropped demand is routed, then reports the physical containers released and exports a multi-tab workbook.
subs.solves: Catalogues grow by accretion, and dropping a reference is safe only if its demand lands on a surviving package that is large enough, valve-compatible, in the same sub-family and margin-neutral, which a spreadsheet cannot enforce across a large catalogue.
subs.edge: There is no direct incumbent for this decision: ERPs hold the master data but do not optimize a substitution network, and the usual alternative is a workshop ranking SKUs by revenue. Results come out as physical container counts released.
moves: Margin protection and feasibility by construction: Each dropped SKU's demand must be conserved, land only on kept SKUs and meet its own margin floor; if the hard model is infeasible, the family re-solves with penalized soft constraints so no family is silently skipped.

Catalogue-shape compression term: A secondary objective weights each product-family by package-format cell at a small fraction of the keep-count term, pushing the solver to empty whole cells rather than merely thin the catalogue.

subs.name: Returnable-Asset Capital Platform
subs.what: An autonomous capital-planning platform for reusable industrial assets such as cylinders, totes, kegs and pallets. It keeps a serialized asset ledger with telemetry, runs a six-agent audit, forecast, budget, optimize, critique and execute pipeline on a timer, solves five CP-SAT models, and routes capital-spend decisions to a human approval cockpit while executing operational actions automatically.
subs.solves: A returnable fleet is a depreciating capital base that nobody owns operationally: renewals tend to go to whoever asks loudest, idle stock sits at customers while depots run short, and requalification is scheduled by due date rather than by risk.
subs.edge: ERP maintenance modules and CMMS tools hold registries and work orders but treat capital allocation as a report, while here five CP-SAT models decide and each response reports engine version, variable and constraint counts and solve time.
moves: CP-SAT presolve tuning: Skipping presolve above a variable-count threshold and supplying a greedy warm start lets large instances solve to optimality in seconds, deterministically, avoiding dominance detection on knapsack structure that otherwise consumed the whole time budget before search began.

Deferral decay and a fixed autonomy boundary: The multi-period model erodes value for late funding so the solver front-loads the riskiest renewals unprompted, while one unit-tested policy constant keeps capital-spend actions from ever being auto-approved.

projects.name: Agentic Supply-Chain Planning Platform
projects.tagline: Agentic sales-and-operations planning for a plant network with LP allocation and a grounded LLM reasoner.
projects.what: A closed-loop, agentic sales and operations planning and execution platform modelled on a multi-plant process-industry network. Demand, tank telemetry, plant capacity, inventory, logistics, finance, plans, exceptions and approvals live in one 40-table database, and every figure on screen is computed from it. Twenty deterministic agents sense the network, a ReAct engine over a local LLM decides, a hard constraint layer validates, and role-based approval mutates plan state to close the loop.
projects.solves: Process plants have turndown, ramp and turnaround limits and power-price structures, while vendor-managed customers show deliveries rather than consumption, so a late confirmation looks like a demand drop and the forecast under-supplies a customer who never reduced usage. The usual alternative is a periodic meeting over emailed spreadsheets that spends its time reconciling numbers instead of deciding.

versus.incumbents: Enterprise planning suites, spreadsheet workbooks passed by email
versus.edge: Unlike enterprise planning suites, this platform models plant physics natively (an LP allocation whose unit cost combines specific energy, a power-price factor and haul), separates delivered volume from telemetry-derived consumption, and adds a groundedness verifier that blocks LLM decisions disproportionate to the evidence they consulted. Its event ledger is hash-chained.

moves: Agentic-primary inversion: An early iteration made the LLM a decision-maker with read-only tools and one structured decision validated by a deterministic constraint layer, and the next demoted the rule-based agents to the sensing layer, so deterministic output is the safety net and advisories promote automatically if the model is unreachable.

Groundedness verifier: Each decision must have consulted its evidence tool and stay proportionate to it, so a large forecast move against a near-flat observed trend is blocked and the deterministic fallback is promoted. Reasoning is serialized through one queue with a wall-clock cap, and boot recovery promotes the advisories of orphaned runs.
LP replacing a heuristic: Production allocation minimizes unit cost plus a large shortfall penalty, bounded by turndown and derate, and returns the single biggest shift move between plants.

One DB layer, two engines: SQLite to PostgreSQL was handled by one async layer, with cutover gated on byte-identical seed statistics and a passing full suite on both engines, and the hash-chained event ledger writes inside an exclusive transaction so concurrent writers cannot fork it.

Scenario scoring: Five plan archetypes are simulated over a multi-week horizon from live balance data and scored with tanh compression, so one enormous margin figure cannot swamp a service consideration.

subs.name: Tolerance-Band Plan Governance
subs.what: A plan-governance layer for the same agentic planning platform, advanced by a formal merge of a feature drop plus an audited fix list. It adds a governance engine with tolerance bands and a frozen execution window, a live-world telemetry heartbeat, an explainability layer and an in-product planning explainer.
subs.solves: Plan nervousness: when any agent, LLM decision or human override can rewrite the forecast, the plan churns into uselessness. Governance keeps revisions bounded, including repeated revisions just inside the tolerance band, which escalate rather than auto-apply.
subs.edge: Where enterprise suites usually implement tolerance bands as an alerting layer, here band governance sits in the write path for every proposer and the frozen window is refused at write time.
moves: Cumulative drift against commit anchors: Revisions are classified against the monthly commit's signed-off demand per product, so a chain of small within-band changes cannot compound past the band unreviewed; within band auto-applies, moderate exceedance routes to review and large exceedance escalates to the executive.

Audited merge of a feature drop: A baseline commit came first, then an audit with both test suites actually executed, a keep-list for behaviour the drop would have regressed, a fix commit for verified defects (including a recompute that overwrote a regional plan with network-wide totals) and a test backfill before any new features.

projects.name: Loading-Loss Vision System
projects.tagline: Real-time CCTV vision system that detects cryogenic vapour venting at fill points and estimates the loss.
projects.what: A real-time computer-vision system that detects cryogenic vapour venting at bulk-liquid loading points. It ingests live CCTV over RTSP or ONVIF, segments the vapour plume inside a per-camera region of interest, corroborates it against process telemetry to separate normal venting from abnormal loss, estimates the product lost, auto-clips the event and raises an acknowledgeable operator alert with a false-positive feedback path.
projects.solves: Product lost as visible vapour at outdoor, often unattended fill points hides inside the noise of the plant mass balance, and inventory reconciliation shows only an aggregate variance with no cause. An operator sees white vapour at every fill and cannot tell a normal vent from a costly one.

versus.incumbents: SCADA alarms, inventory reconciliation, operator rounds, generic video analytics, optical gas imaging
versus.edge: There is no direct incumbent: SCADA shows that a valve opened rather than that product left, and generic video analytics are trained on people and vehicles.
