This is a continuous on-prem monitor on existing cameras that fuses process signals with the video, uses a transparent loss model and an operator feedback path.

moves: Four signals must agree: The cold-start classical segmenter requires brightness, low saturation, turbulence and a large connected blob inside the region of interest, so sky, white tanks and snow each fail at least one signal.

Exponentially weighted background: The turbulence map uses an exponentially weighted running mean instead of conventional background subtraction, because a continuously venting plume would be learned into the background and vanish.

Classical detector bootstraps a learned student: The validated classical segmenter auto-labels frames to fine-tune a YOLO11n-seg model, which attaches to a camera with one API call while region, persistence and fusion stay unchanged.

Normal vent versus abnormal loss: Fusion with pressure, valve and flow signals classifies each plume, only abnormal loss opens an event, and a same-camera event resolved within a dedupe window re-opens instead of spawning an alert storm.

Transparent loss model: Plume area converts to volume, mass and rate, integrated over elapsed wall-clock time so dropped frames do not under-count, with every constant held in a per-camera calibration so operators can trust the figure.
proof: 2,314 lines of Python across seven modules plus a training script

projects.name: Offline Windows Deployment Package
projects.tagline: Offline Windows packaging that runs a routing and capital platform with embedded truck-aware routing.
projects.what: A packaged snapshot of the routing and capital-planning platforms, plus the offline-distribution engineering behind it. A build script produces a zip64 archive that a user with no internet, no admin rights and no Docker can extract and launch by double-clicking a batch file. The package carries a private Python, offline wheels, the prebuilt UI and a regional routing tile extract, and sets itself up on first launch.
projects.solves: Enterprise laptops often lack Docker, admin rights, Python and open network access, and delivery data containing customer details cannot go to a cloud routing API. That rules out both paid routing APIs and Docker-hosted self-hosted routing, which this package replaces with a single archive.

versus.incumbents: Hosted SaaS trials, Docker Compose stacks, pip packages, MSI installers
versus.edge: Where each incumbent needs data egress, admin rights, internet access or code signing, this needs only extracting a zip and double-clicking a batch file. Routing runs in-process on a bundled tile extract, so delivery data never leaves the machine.

moves: Docker Valhalla to in-process pyvalhalla: An actor pool replaced the Docker service behind an adapter-exact API, so the provider code path, chunking, retry and caching are unchanged; a pool is needed because routing actors are not free-threaded and the solver runs many parallel group workers.

Service limits tuned on measurement: Stock matrix and distance limits declined a large share of big routing groups under strict road-true mode, so the limits were raised while request chunking still bounds each request.

Archive strategy: Zip64 carries a payload beyond the classic 4 GB limit, and the tile tar is STORED while everything else is DEFLATED, since compressing an already compact binary store spends build time for no gain.

Launcher pre-flight: The batch launcher counts its own install path length and refuses to proceed beyond a safe maximum, and verifies the tile file is present, so a Windows path-length problem is caught up front instead of surfacing as an obscure Python error hours later.

projects.name: Digester and RNG Plant Simulators
projects.tagline: Interactive digital twins that let RNG developers and digester operators watch process trade-offs move live.
projects.what: Two desktop simulators for biogas and renewable natural gas work. One is a 3D digital twin of a landfill-gas-to-RNG plant driven by a time-accelerated process model; the other is an operator-console twin of a mesophilic anaerobic digester with gauges, live trends and manual overrides.
projects.solves: RNG developers normally chain four disconnected tools (a regulatory generation workbook, a wellfield spreadsheet, a vendor sizing tool and a financial model), so changing one assumption means re-running everything by hand. Digester operators lose reactors to acid crash, a slow failure that is invisible on a single reading and hard to build intuition for. The twins fold that chain into one live model and let operators watch an acid crash develop on screen.

versus.incumbents: EPA LandGEM workbook, commercial process simulators, open ADM1 implementations, vendor SCADA and sizing tools
versus.edge: The landfill twin runs the same first-order decay physics as LandGEM at sub-day resolution and carries the result through collection, gas composition and membrane separation, so methane slip versus purity moves live with the sliders. The digester twin is a deliberately reduced four-state model built for operator intuition, with zero third-party dependencies. Unlike a chain of spreadsheets and vendor tools, both put the cause-and-effect loop in front of the user in real time.

moves: LandGEM cohort ring buffer: Replaced a closed-form lump model, which ages all waste as if it were placed at once, with 732 monthly cohorts (60-year horizon) in a fixed-size ring buffer, evaluating the decay summation as one vectorised NumPy reduction per tick so an active landfill ages correctly.

Wellfield coupling: Vacuum and well density jointly set collection efficiency and oxygen ingress, and the resulting inert fraction degrades the membrane separation factor, so the operator dilemma of pulling harder versus pulling cleaner shows up as one number.
Closed balances: The plant model closes methane and CO2 balances across the membrane skid and reports CH4 slip, CO2 vent, MMBtu/day and CO2e avoided (GWP 28) together.

Asset pipeline migration: Replaced a dependency on a 2.3 GB open-source landscape asset library with a 53-line deterministic generator that drives headless Blender to build multi-fractal terrain, with smart-UV unwrap and height-derived vertex colours.

Emergent acid crash: In the digester twin, a feed-rate threshold falls out of acid load competing with buffer recovery, and a pH efficiency cliff converts it into a production collapse and a methane drop, rather than being scripted as a rule.

subs.name: Landfill-to-RNG Plant Digital Twin
subs.what: A desktop 3D digital twin of a landfill-gas-to-RNG plant: wellfield, knock-out drum, H2S vessel, membrane skid, compressor and flare animated by a time-accelerated process model. Sliders move landfill and upgrading parameters, pipes recolour by flow, tagged sensors turn red on alarm and the scene flashes when the plant goes off-spec.
subs.solves: Shows how waste mass, collection efficiency, air ingress and membrane stage count jointly set methane slip, product purity and output, without re-running four separate models.
subs.edge: Compared with the annual, generation-only LandGEM workbook and black-box vendor sizing tools, it is live and exposes the recovery versus purity trade-off as the sliders move.
moves: Closed-form to cohort model: Moved from a core that applied one age to all waste to a 732-slot monthly cohort buffer that sums k * L0 * mass * exp(-k * age) in one NumPy pass, with fixed memory however long the run.

Numerical guards: Every division carries an epsilon and every physical input is clamped, because a slider-driven simulator visits the entire input space and the model has to stay valid at the extremes.

subs.name: Digester Operator Console Twin
subs.what: A single-file Tkinter operator console for a mesophilic anaerobic digester. A 100 ms physics loop advances tank temperature, pH, biogas flow and methane fraction, shown on donut gauges and sparklines with sliders for feed rate, target temperature and mixer speed.
subs.solves: Gives operators intuition for acid crash, where overfeeding drops pH, inhibits methanogens and sours the gas.
subs.edge: A zero-dependency, reduced-order model of four states and three multiplicative efficiency terms stands in for ADM1's 26 states or licensed simulators, keeping the behaviour that matters to an operator in one readable file.
moves: Multiplicative efficiencies: Gas yield is the product of a Gaussian temperature term, a pH cliff and a saturating mixing term, so three tolerable deviations compound into an intolerable one, as in real digesters.

Canvas widget toolkit: Tkinter has no gauge or chart primitives, so both were built from canvas geometry, with tag-scoped partial redraw keeping 10 Hz animation flicker-free and fixed-size history buffers.

projects.name: Landfill RNG Opportunity Screening Toolkit
projects.tagline: Screens, scores and forecasts RNG potential across US landfills from public EPA data.
projects.what: A three-part toolkit built on EPA public data: a Streamlit explorer over the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program landfill tables, a Django REST and React portal over the LMOP landfill database with scoring and forecasting, and a notebook suite that applies first-order decay modelling to every landfill in that database. Together they rank landfills by methane potential and map the developers and owners behind the best sites.
projects.solves: The EPA publishes the data for a national map of landfill-gas opportunity, but as normalised tables and a wide spreadsheet with no ranking, joins or market context. Subscription market-intelligence products repackage the same free data. Sites with no reported collected-gas figure, the greenfield set, are also invisible to spreadsheet filtering.

versus.incumbents: EPA data portals, the LMOP spreadsheet, subscription market-intelligence products, manual research
versus.edge: Scoring rules are short readable code rather than an opaque vendor model, and the physics (methane flow, first-order decay) ranks sites before any commercial layer is attached. Technical merit and market sentiment are kept as two separate scores instead of one unexplainable number. Unlike products that repackage the same free data, every ranking traces back to public EPA inputs.

moves: Scoring evolved to a flow-only rule: The opportunity classifier moved from matching firm names against lists of known companies, to a composite string of firm tag and flow band, to a flow-only rule on methane flow (SCFM x 60 x CH4 fraction), so a small site never outranks a far larger one and incomplete records stay visible by mapping Unknown to Low.

Fan-out collapse in EPA joins: Child tables with many rows per facility are group-aggregated into pipe-delimited strings before the left join, so facilities are not duplicated on the map or double-counted for flow.
Reported-else-calculated gas estimate: Reported collected gas is used where present and a first-order decay calculation otherwise, which ranks greenfield sites on the same axis as operating ones.

Scalar to auditable forecast: A schema migration changed the forecast from a single number into three forecast years, a confidence score, market sentiment and the full structured payload, with the original field kept for compatibility.

Explainable technical score: A multi-factor, multi-category 0-100 rubric accumulates earned and available points so the denominator adjusts and the result is a true normalised percentage. It was chosen over a learned model so that each point is defensible to a reviewer.
proof: Django 5 REST backend with a React 19 portal

subs.name: EPA Landfill Data Explorer
subs.what: A multi-page Streamlit app that pulls EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program Subpart HH landfill tables live, merges them into one facility table, bands every facility by methane flow and maps them on a pydeck US map. It also generates per-facility business-development briefs with Google Gemini, exportable to a Word document.
subs.solves: EPA's landfill data is five normalised tables behind a paginated JSON endpoint with no map, ranking or join.
subs.edge: It offers free public data and a scoring rule readable in about 40 lines in place of subscription market-intelligence products.
moves: Session caching for slow, billable calls: Streamlit reruns the script on every interaction, so the merged EPA frame lives in session state and Gemini output is a write-through cache. The work queue is a set-difference against enriched IDs in batches, and an uploaded CSV can re-seed the cache.
Null-safe prompt building: Prompt bullets are emitted only for non-null fields so the model never sees nan, and a fixed six-section output format is pinned.

subs.name: Landfill Asset Scoring Portal
subs.what: A Django 5 REST backend and React 19 single-page app over the EPA LMOP landfill database and a national wastewater plant dataset. It computes a deterministic 0-100 technical score per site and, on request, a three-year production forecast with sentiment, risks and citations from a search-grounded Gemini call, shown on a Leaflet asset map.
subs.solves: In the LMOP spreadsheet, technical merit and market signal never meet, and no analyst can research thousands of sites by hand.
subs.edge: It keeps a deterministic technical score separate from an evidence-based sentiment score with a confidence value.
moves: Polymorphic forecast table: Nullable foreign keys to landfills and wastewater plants let one table and one serializer serve two asset classes.

Failure handling: A three-attempt retry with backoff, markdown-fence stripping, a shape check on the first forecast year and a neutral fallback object keep the API responding when the model is unavailable.

subs.name: First-Order Decay Screening Notebooks
subs.what: A four-notebook pipeline that rebuilds the EPA LMOP database from primary ArcGIS feature services and computes first-order-decay gas potential for every landfill in it. It then maps the surviving sites to the developers and owners behind them in multi-sheet Excel workbooks.
subs.solves: Landfills without a gas project report no collected-gas figure, so filtering on reported data hides greenfield sites, and a ranked site list is not actionable until the organisations behind the sites are identified.
subs.edge: It runs a national batch screen where the standard LandGEM workbook models one landfill at a time and consultant models are paid per site.
moves: Three gas estimators: A rule of thumb (a fixed rate per million tons, age-blind) gave way to first-order decay with EPA defaults (k 0.05, L0 170 m3/Mg), then to a hybrid that uses reported collected gas where present and the calculation otherwise.

Entity matching without fuzzy matching: Company names are lowercased and stripped of punctuation and trailing legal suffixes, which collapses name variants without a fuzzy matcher's false positives; ArcGIS offset pagination at 2,000 records per page rebuilds the full database.

projects.name: Facility Lead Scoring Dashboard
projects.tagline: Ranks industrial facilities as sales leads with ML scoring, live EPA data and on-demand dossiers.
projects.what: A Streamlit dashboard that unifies several source workbooks into one lead schema of numeric attributes, augments them live from the EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, scores every facility with TabPFN and maps and ranks them within facility groups. On demand it generates a structured, search-grounded competitive dossier per lead with a PDF download.
projects.solves: Sales teams for an industrial product line must decide which facilities merit a call, but public sources share no schema, scale unit or identifier, and size means different things for different facility types. The competitive context that decides deals is scattered across trade press, filings and permits and goes stale quickly.

versus.incumbents: Subscription market-intelligence products, purchased contact lists in a CRM, analyst desk research, spreadsheet scoring
versus.edge: Unlike purchased lists and subscription products, it generates the lead universe from free regulatory data and scores it on facility physics, with group-relative percentile ranking making unlike facility types comparable and TabPFN returning a probability. The score works as a prioritisation signal, so a sales team sees which facilities deserve a call first. Live EPA augmentation keeps the facility attributes tied to the regulatory source.

moves: Calibrated scoring from a continuous index: A hard threshold on an opportunity index would teach a classifier to memorise the rule. Instead a continuous index, re-ranked within each group, feeds Bernoulli proxy labels drawn from a logistic function of the index, so classes overlap and the model learns a calibrated posterior.

TabPFN for calibrated probabilities: A prior-data-fitted transformer gives calibrated probabilities without hyperparameter search. Training uses a class-balanced sample within the model's row limit and a small ensemble, and the full lead set is scored in batches on CPU on first load, then cached.

False-match defences in the EPA connector: Organisations skip facility matching, substring matches need a minimum length, matching never falls back to a nationwide search, and leads without a state need a higher similarity cutoff. The connector also checks content type, because the EPA service answers unknown paths with an HTTP 200 HTML page.
Status reconciliation: A facility whose prior gas project ended is reclassified as a new opportunity instead of being read as closed, a distinction the raw status field obscures.
Role-aware dossier generation: The dossier generator detects whether a lead is an end-user site or an intermediary and adapts its prompt and structure accordingly.

projects.name: Resumable Contact Discovery Scraper
projects.tagline: Resumable pipeline that finds organisation websites and public-profile contacts for a registry of assets.
projects.what: A resumable Selenium pipeline that takes asset records from a public registry and, for each one, finds the owning organisation's website and a capped number of named contacts from public professional-profile search results. It uses one query strategy for government owners and another for corporations, and companion notebooks match discovered organisations to a public partner directory with TF-IDF similarity.
projects.solves: Many assets are owned by public bodies, where the right person sits in a department whose name varies by jurisdiction and is not in the data, so a corporate-style query returns nothing. Commercial contact databases cover municipal departments poorly, and manual research is too slow to be practical at registry scale.

versus.incumbents: Commercial contact databases, manual research, paid search APIs, generic scrapers
versus.edge: Contacts are discovered from the asset record with a government-specific query ladder, and each row keeps its source URL and title so every contact traces back to a public result. Unlike generic scrapers that run one corporate-style query, the strategy adapts to owner type and escalates only as far as each record needs.

moves: Owner-aware search strategy: Moved from a single corporate-tuned query to a strategy selected by owner type, crossing department terms with seniority titles into an escalating query ladder and preferring government web domains for public owners.
Escalation with a cap: Queries run in order and stop once enough distinct person profiles are found, so hard records get more attempts than easy ones while cost per record stays bounded.

Resumability and safe scheduling: The output file doubles as the checkpoint and is flushed per batch, so a crash loses at most one batch, and a lock-file mutex stops overlapping scheduled runs from scraping the same rows twice.

Exact matching to TF-IDF: Moved organisation matching from exact strings to TF-IDF character similarity so name variants resolve, with a tuned cutoff and an evaluation cell reporting matched rows to make the precision and recall trade-off visible. One vectorised matrix product replaces an O(n*m) edit-distance loop.
Interchangeable search engines: Three engines sit behind one dispatcher, so switching engines is a one-line change rather than a rewrite.
proof: three search engines behind one dispatcher

projects.name: Landfill Gas Document Extraction Pipeline
projects.tagline: Finds public landfill-gas project documents and extracts project facts with a local LLM on GPU.
projects.what: A batch pipeline that searches government sites for landfill-gas project documents (RFPs, permit applications, board minutes, solid-waste plans, grant notices), downloads them, extracts text with PyMuPDF and pulls project-level facts into CSV using a locally hosted Mistral 7B Instruct model on GPU. A separate Selenium scraper extracts every table from EPA GHG detailed facility reports.
projects.solves: Early signals of landfill-gas projects are often PDFs on county websites, scattered across many domains, written in prose and published without notification. Bid-monitoring services cover formal solicitations but not board minutes or management plans.

versus.incumbents: Bid-monitoring services, web alert services, manual monitoring, commercial LLM APIs
versus.edge: Site-restricted queries across 15 templates also catch informal documents such as board minutes and management plans, and a local model means no per-token cost and no document content leaving the machine. Documents stream through in fixed 1,024-character slices with per-chunk extraction appended to CSV, so even a long plan is processed in bounded memory.

moves: GPU memory migration: Moved from Llama 3.1 8B at full precision with no chunking to Mistral 7B Instruct with cache clearing before load, an expandable-segments allocator setting, explicit device placement with CPU fallback, FP16 autocast and hard truncation at 1,024 tokens, so long batches finish without out-of-memory failures.

Chunked streaming: Documents are split into fixed 1,024-character slices with per-chunk extraction and CSV append, so a long management plan is processed as a stream with bounded memory. SQLite persistence was dropped in favour of CSV append.
Second recency gate: Search-engine date filters are unreliable on PDFs, which often carry no usable date, so results are also filtered on a year found in the snippet text.

Layout-agnostic table scraper: The facility-report scraper takes every h4 header and its next sibling table instead of hard-coded paths, stamping facility ID, source and table title, so a report redesign adds tables rather than breaking the scraper.

projects.name: Emission Report Archive Batching Utility
projects.tagline: Batching utility that prepares landfill surface-emission compliance report PDFs for downstream extraction.
projects.what: A small standard-library utility that copies surface emission monitoring (SEM) report PDFs into fixed-size batch folders for downstream document extraction. It is paired with an organised archive of quarterly and annual landfill compliance reports.
projects.solves: Under EPA landfill NSPS and emission guidelines, operators walk the surface each quarter and record readings of 500 ppm methane or more as exceedances. The useful longitudinal question, which zones exceed repeatedly and whether counts trend upward, spans dozens of PDFs per site and many years and is rarely answered, so remediation stays reactive. Rising exceedances can also point to an under-performing gas collection system.

versus.incumbents: No direct incumbent; consultants, wellfield software, state portals and GHGRP each cover part
versus.edge: No off-the-shelf tool does longitudinal SEM analysis: consultants deliver PDFs, wellfield software tracks wellhead readings, agency portals publish without aggregating, and GHGRP Subpart HH covers modelled rather than scan data. This utility starts that analysis by turning a report collection into evenly sized batches ready for extraction.

moves: Non-destructive batching: Files are copied with metadata preserved rather than moved, because modification times can be the only reliable chronology on a collection whose filename conventions drifted over the years.
Fixed-size partitioning: The utility creates ceil(n/10) subfolders of 10 files each, matching the per-batch limits of document-extraction tools and model context windows.

Defensive file handling: Source validation returns a plain message instead of a traceback, an empty collection triggers a warning, and errors on listing, directory creation and each file are caught so one unreadable PDF does not abort a run.
Revision history as signal: Draft, final and revised filename suffixes record agency review and resubmit cycles, the kind of pattern a longitudinal exceedance analysis can surface.

projects.name: Clean-Technology Scouting Backend
projects.tagline: Self-hosted FastAPI backend that tracks clean-tech startups and documents with full audit provenance.
projects.what: An async FastAPI service on PostgreSQL 16 with SQLAlchemy 2 and Alembic that ingests startup data through provider adapters, parses PDFs and runs schema-constrained structured extraction with Gemini through a versioned prompt registry. Every ingested record and every model call carries provenance. The code follows a strict routers, services, repositories and models layering.
projects.solves: Industrial companies scouting clean technology need to know which startups are credible candidates and at what readiness level, but assessments from subscriptions and slide decks cannot be audited months later: nothing records what was read, which model or prompt produced a score, or what the raw source said. The same startup also appears under several names and domains across feeds, and merging by hand loses the raw payloads.

versus.incumbents: Startup-database and market-intelligence subscriptions, shared drives of PDFs, ad-hoc LLM scripts
versus.edge: It is self-hosted, with a technology taxonomy and maturity scale the user defines, relevance scored against the user's own asset base, and every assessment stored with its inputs. Unlike subscriptions and slide decks, any score can be traced months later to the source, model and prompt version that produced it.

moves: Deterministic deduplication: A SHA-256 key over a normalised name and domain, enforced by a database unique constraint, makes upserts idempotent. It was chosen over fuzzy matching, which would need a threshold and a review queue, and raw payloads are kept so canonical records can be re-derived when merge logic changes.
Idempotent ingestion: Key-order-independent payload hashing lets an unchanged record be skipped before any work is done, so re-running ingestion is a safe no-op.

Dual-sided schema enforcement: Pydantic models serve as both the model's response schema and the database-boundary validator, with bounded scores, enums and lists that are never null. Prompts are versioned and old versions stay resident so past audit rows remain interpretable.

Audit chokepoint: One run row per model call, success or failure, records model, prompt name and version, raw and parsed response, validation status, latency and error, and stored extractions reference it with a restrict-on-delete foreign key.

Retry policy by error class: Rate limits, server errors and transport failures retry with exponential backoff while schema violations do not, and per-attempt timeouts give a computable wall-time bound of timeout x (retries + 1).

projects.name: Patent Mining and RAG Toolkit
projects.tagline: Mines public patent data for process parameters with an LLM and lays out a self-hosted RAG stack.
projects.what: A patent-mining pipeline harvests a patent portfolio from public patent data, retrieves full claims and descriptions, extracts process parameters into structured CSVs with Gemini and renders them as interactive force-directed knowledge graphs. Alongside it sits a five-service self-hosted infrastructure stack for a document-grounded technical knowledge assistant.
projects.solves: Manufacturing process know-how is rarely published as a whole, but fragments are disclosed in claims and worked examples across many patents. Large assignees file across many unrelated businesses, so an assignee search returns a huge result set with a small relevant share, and neither reading it nor keyword filtering is feasible.

versus.incumbents: Commercial patent-analytics suites, public patent search interfaces, consultants
versus.edge: Patent-analytics suites cover landscape statistics but not process parameters such as temperatures and chemical additives, which sit in worked examples. This pipeline triages relevance, then extracts exact numbers and chemicals across fixed extraction categories into a directly comparable matrix. The companion stack keeps the corpus self-hosted so only the generation call leaves the machine.

moves: Query narrowing: A conjunction of assignee, topic, material and process-step clauses cut a broad sweep to a far smaller targeted set. The process-step clause separates patents describing how a product is made from those that merely mention it.

Three retrieval backends: Migrated from a plain HTTP client against a patent site to a browser-emulating client and finally to the public Google patents dataset on BigQuery, which brings no rate limit or CAPTCHA and clean claims and description fields.

Application-number hardening: Google Patents CSV exports drop a zero from 20xx-series US application numbers, so the code re-inserts it before lookups and uses separate LIKE patterns for published applications and granted patents.
Triage then deep extraction: A cheap relevance classification runs first and expensive full extraction only on survivors, with a local Gemma 3 pass explored for running the triage stage on-premises.
Fixed-column extraction: The most disciplined output maps fixed columns one-to-one onto the extraction targets, giving a directly comparable matrix instead of prose.

subs.name: Patent Parameter Extraction Notebooks
subs.what: A notebook pipeline that harvests a patent portfolio, retrieves full text and extracts process parameters across fixed manufacturing stages into CSVs. The results are rendered as vis-network knowledge graphs, one using a Barnes-Hut solver and one using a second force-directed layout.
subs.solves: Process-level detail is buried in claims and worked examples across a very large, mostly irrelevant patent portfolio.
subs.edge: It goes beyond the landscape analytics of subscription patent tools by extracting exact parameters.
moves: Process-step query clause: Adding manufacturing-step terms to the Boolean query cut the result set sharply and selects patents that describe making a product, not just mentioning one.

Backend migration: Scraping a patent site gave way to a browser-emulating client and finally to the public patents dataset on BigQuery, with separate matching patterns for published applications and granted patents.

subs.name: Self-Hosted RAG Infrastructure Stack
subs.what: A five-service Docker Compose stack for a retrieval-augmented technical knowledge assistant: Qdrant vector database, S3-compatible object storage, GROBID scientific-PDF parser, FastAPI backend and Node frontend, with pinned Python dependencies.
subs.solves: Engineering design answers such as material properties live in tables inside papers, patents and datasheets, which generic PDF text extraction destroys.
subs.edge: It commits to structure-preserving GROBID parsing and a self-hosted corpus where only the generation call leaves the machine, versus manual literature search, general chat models and hosted RAG services.
moves: GROBID isolated in its own container: A parser trained on scholarly documents preserves sections, references and tables, and its 3 GB JVM heap runs as a separate always-restarting service rather than a library inside the API.

Corpus separate from index: Original PDFs sit in object storage and embeddings in Qdrant on mounted volumes, so the index can be rebuilt after a chunking change without re-acquiring documents, with matched Qdrant server and client versions.

projects.name: Lead Consolidation and Ranking Pipeline
projects.tagline: Consolidates public directories and company registers into one ranked, contact-tiered lead workbook.
projects.what: A Python scraping and consolidation pipeline for lead qualification in an industrial product line. It codifies product-fit categories with application and fit rules, sources companies from industrial directories and national company registers, and enriches websites for published contact details. Everything is consolidated into one ranked master workbook.
projects.solves: Each lead needs a technical qualification against product-fit criteria that generic lists cannot express. The national registers that hold the right companies are huge files with no websites or contacts.

versus.incumbents: Commercial contact databases, purchased lists, email-finder services, spreadsheet lead management
versus.edge: Each category carries its application, purchase rationale, technical-fit verdict and target titles, and contactability is tiered, with the top tier carrying a named person and email. Unlike purchased lists, every lead is scored on product fit first and contact completeness second.

moves: Checkpointed multi-stage pipeline: Separate stages per source family, then dedupe-score-rank, hand off through pickle files, so a change to one category's tier mapping re-runs one stage instead of re-parsing every source workbook.
Tiering and scoring: Contact-completeness tiers use source-specific rules, and the priority score is a fit weight plus a tier bonus, capped at 100, so fit dominates and contactability breaks ties.

Found versus inferred contacts: Website enrichment visits a few pages per site, classifies emails as role, junk or personal, and keeps an inferred generic address in its own column so found contacts stay clean.
Several taxonomies, one target set: Industry codes from different national classification schemes were mapped onto one category taxonomy, reducing a very large register to a small target set.

Contact-name validity filter: Length, digit, word-count and a junk-term pattern separate real people from organisation names in EPA facility contact fields, and both raw and validated counts are reported.

projects.name: National Wastewater Plant Biosolids Dataset
projects.tagline: Rebuildable US wastewater plant dataset with biosolids permits and site contacts, built from EPA sources.
projects.what: A national wastewater treatment plant dataset and its build pipeline: a three-stage notebook that constructs a standardised schema for every US wastewater facility from the EPA ECHO exporter, adds NPDES and biosolids permit detail from bulk downloads, then scrapes the EPA Facility Registry Service for owner, operator and site contact of the biosolids subset. The output is four CSVs, the largest covering 58,607 facilities.
projects.solves: Municipal wastewater plants with digesters are a biogas source, and a biosolids permit is the best public proxy for having digesters. No single EPA product says which plants exist, which hold biosolids permits and who runs them: ECHO does not identify wastewater plants as such, permit data sits in separate files, and registry contacts exist only on per-ID web pages.

versus.incumbents: EPA ECHO web query, purchased plant lists, CWNS survey, manual registry lookups
versus.edge: The whole set is built from public EPA sources and can be rebuilt at any time, with a biosolids flag, NPDES linkage and named contacts that purchased lists lack. Unlike a one-off ECHO query or manual registry lookups, one notebook run narrows 58,607 facilities to the 6,635 biosolids facilities with contacts.

moves: Narrowing funnel: The build goes from 58,607 facilities to 58,607 permit-enriched facilities to 6,635 biosolids facilities with contacts. Registry scraping for everyone would be 58,607 requests at 0.4 s (about 6.5 hours), so the expensive stage runs only on the qualified subset.

Wastewater identification: A facility qualifies by NPDES flag or one of nine name keywords, including WATER RESOURCE RECOVERY and WRRF, the modern renaming of a treatment plant that a naive WWTP filter would miss.
Streaming ingestion: The national zip archive is streamed in memory and read in 200,000-row chunks with per-chunk filtering, so memory is bounded by the chunk and no temporary file is written.
Cache-backed scraping: A persistent CSV cache keyed on a normalised registry ID makes re-runs free, and stripping the trailing .0 that float inference leaves on IDs keeps every request well-formed.

projects.name: Real-Time Geospatial Intelligence Platform
projects.tagline: Open-source dashboard fork that scores public EPA registry sites into daily-diffed, explainable sales leads.
projects.what: Extends an open-source real-time geospatial dashboard with a domain fork that re-points it at public-data lead scoring. The fork's own contribution is a new Python scoring service that turns public EPA landfill and wastewater registries into a ranked, geolocated list of sales leads using vectorised distance-and-policy scoring and day-over-day diffing, with a React/Leaflet panel as the front-end direction.
projects.solves: Qualifying an industrial site means combining scale, infrastructure and policy facts that live in different places, and a hand-refreshed spreadsheet never shows what changed since yesterday. The service gathers those facts into one scored, mapped list and reports each day which sites are new, rising or dropped.

versus.incumbents: Spreadsheets, contact-centric sales databases, announced-project trackers and generic map dashboards
versus.edge: Unlike spreadsheets, contact-centric sales databases or announced-project trackers, the unit of analysis is the facility, scored before any announcement and with its reasons attached. Starting from an existing map dashboard shell, the fork puts its effort into the scoring logic and the daily change view rather than into rebuilding a map stack.

moves: Domain re-pointing: Re-aimed the existing dashboard shell from geopolitical monitoring to public-registry lead scoring, adding a Python backend that supplies ranked, geolocated leads and a React/Leaflet panel as the presentation direction.

Rule engine over a model: With no outcome history, a fitted model would fit noise, so an additive rubric clipped to a fixed range is used and stays arguable in a sales meeting; a distance penalty for far-off infrastructure outweighs any positive term, encoding a near-veto.
Vectorised scoring: Distance and policy terms are computed as vectorised operations, so each registry is scored as a batch rather than site by site.
Snapshot diffing: Daily snapshots keyed by source and id yield new, rising and dropped buckets, and a minimum score-rise threshold filters out noise such as a news cache expiring.
proof: 2 public EPA registries (landfill and wastewater) scored
Additive rubric over site scale, infrastructure proximity and regional policy
Daily snapshots with new, rising and dropped buckets

subs.name: Public-Data Lead-Scoring Service
subs.what: A FastAPI service that turns two public US EPA registries into a ranked, geolocated, day-over-day-diffed list of sales leads for an industrial equipment product line. Each site is scored on a transparent additive rubric of site scale, infrastructure proximity and regional policy, boosted by matching news, and snapshotted daily.
subs.solves: Qualifying a site means combining several facts held in different places, and a spreadsheet plus news alerts is refreshed by hand and never shows what changed since yesterday.
subs.edge: Unlike spreadsheets, contact-centric sales databases or announced-project trackers, the unit of analysis is the facility, scored before any announcement and with its reasons attached.
moves: Rule engine over a model: With no outcome history, a fitted model would fit noise, so an additive rubric clipped to a fixed range is used and stays arguable in a sales meeting; a distance penalty for far-off infrastructure outweighs any positive term, encoding a near-veto.
Snapshot diffing: Daily snapshots keyed by source and id yield new, rising and dropped buckets, and a minimum score-rise threshold filters out noise such as a news cache expiring.

projects.name: Agentic Quoting Copilot and ML Engine
projects.tagline: Agentic quoting copilot over 17 MCP tools, paired with a calibrated, time-split ML decision engine.
projects.what: A two-part engineering-sales system for configurable industrial products. The copilot takes a free-text customer specification and, using four MCP tool servers that expose business, compliance, engineering and historical-learning data as 17 tools, either produces a costed, rule-compliant quote or routes a structured brief to engineering. The ML engine is a deterministic state-machine agent that trains and evaluates six tabular decision models and streams every step to a live dashboard.
projects.solves: Quoting a configurable technical product touches an ERP, approved-component lists, CAD, past projects and pricing rules that do not talk to each other, and the costly failure is a confidently wrong quote, such as a bill of materials containing a component with no valid certification. On the modelling side, random splits, aggregate metrics and uncalibrated probabilities let weak models slip through.

versus.incumbents: Product-configurator and CPQ suites, AutoML platforms, direct ERP queries, spreadsheets and tribal knowledge
versus.edge: Configurators answer whether a configuration is valid, while here the agent chooses which tools to call and whether to quote at all, sending novel requests to engineering with a structured hand-off. AutoML platforms optimise on random splits, whereas the ML engine uses time-split holdouts, isotonic calibration and slice-regression checks before any promotion decision.

moves: MCP topology: Four separate MCP servers with 6, 3, 4 and 4 tools are aggregated by a multi-client that gives the model one flat 17-tool namespace. Hardened the transport by passing the already-parsed request body explicitly to the SDK instead of letting it re-read a consumed stream.

Provider-agnostic tool use: Anthropic content blocks, OpenAI tool calls and Gemini function-role history are normalised behind one streaming interface, so swapping the reasoning model is an environment-variable change.

Handling invented identifiers: Because the model routinely invents plausible part identifiers, a two-layer scored fuzzy fallback (identifier prefix, name similarity) and a scored proxy bill-of-materials selector resolve them, with every substitution recorded in the trace instead of applied silently.

Chunked TabPFN: TabPFN's bounded context cannot see a large training set, so the champion is bagged over quantile-balanced stratified subsamples sized to that context, fitted and averaged, with the wrapper kept thin to stay robust to churn in the upstream package.

Planted-drift benchmark: A synthetic relational database embeds a deliberate performance drop in one segment inside the holdout window; the slice evaluator flagged a regression beyond its sigma threshold, worst on that segment, showing the promotion gate catches segment-level problems that aggregate metrics hide.
proof: Six model specs declared as YAML
Three LLM provider formats behind one streaming interface

subs.name: Agentic Quoting Copilot
subs.what: An agentic quoting system: a free-text specification goes to a reasoning agent wired to four MCP tool servers exposing 17 tools, and it returns a costed, rule-compliant quote or a structured engineering brief. Every reasoning step and tool call streams to the browser over Server-Sent Events, so the trace on screen is the actual decision path.
subs.solves: Quoting configurable technical products by hand spans several disconnected systems and risks confidently wrong quotes, or quotes for requests that are really engineering projects.
subs.edge: Unlike rule-engine configurators or direct ERP queries, the model decides tool order per request and a hand-off path to engineering exists, and every tool response carries an A to D provenance grade showing how production-ready its data source is. The agent and database run locally.
moves: Auditable pricing and enrichment: Pricing returns its full computation trace (BOM roll-up, tier multiplier, surcharges) rather than a bare number, and when the agent skips the BOM lookup the orchestrator calls it itself and logs it as a real tool call flagged as automatic, with measured latency.

Zero-copy retrieval: Past-case embeddings are stored as raw float bytes in SQLite and read as a Float32Array view with no JSON parse, and a cosine-similarity floor returns nothing below it, which is the signal that a request is novel.

subs.name: Autonomous Model-Development Engine
subs.what: An autonomous model-development service. Six tabular prediction problems are declared as YAML specs with SQL, metric and promotion threshold, then run through a state-machine agent that probes feature recipes, trains XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM baselines and a chunked TabPFN champion, calibrates, slice-evaluates and decides.
subs.solves: Random splits, aggregate metrics and uncalibrated probabilities hide the failures that matter, such as a model that is worst on its least reliable segment.
subs.edge: Versus AutoML leaderboards or a notebook per problem, the methodology is declarative data with time-split holdouts, isotonic calibration and a 2-sigma slice flag before promotion.
moves: Feature recipes: A JSON vocabulary (cyclic sin and cos for month, target encoding, rolling statistics) has candidates proposed by an LLM and judged on the holdout over a bounded number of rounds, so the proposer suggests and the data decides.

Calibration and splits: Time-split holdouts anchored on a cutoff date replace k-fold because every target is a forecast, and isotonic calibration is used over Platt scaling because it assumes no sigmoid miscalibration.

projects.name: Procedural Blender Digital Twin
projects.tagline: Procedural Blender model of an industrial equipment room, GPU-rendered and shipped as a web viewer.
projects.what: A procedurally built, GPU-rendered 3D model of an on-premises equipment room in an industrial setting: server racks, a compute node with its lid off, network security gear, power and switching hardware and colour-coded cabling, matched line by line to a hardware bill of materials. It exports to binary glTF for an interactive web viewer and renders stills and 4K walkthrough videos for slide decks. A multi-volume HTML field guide to the surrounding OT/IT stack accompanies it.
projects.solves: Placing new compute hardware near an industrial process means convincing operations, controls engineering and IT security, who share no vocabulary. A 2D rack elevation cannot answer their spatial questions, and a device whose whole value is physical behaviour, such as enforcing a one-way boundary, looks like any other box on it. The model makes that visible to people who will never read the relevant standard.

versus.incumbents: Industrial digital-twin platforms, BIM review tools, infrastructure-management 3D views, game engines and 2D rack-elevation diagrams
versus.edge: Free Blender plus a few-megabyte GLB in a model-viewer page opens in any browser, where twin platforms, licensed infrastructure-management tools and game-engine bundles are heavier. It is built as a communication artefact for a proposed installation, so detail is component-level exactly where the argument needs it.

moves: Materials before geometry: Upgraded all 81 default-shader materials in place with per-category PBR values, which transformed the look with no new geometry, since fan logos, gold connector fingers and keymarks were already modelled.

Parenting hardening: Fixed placement of text on an in-scene monitor by resetting a non-identity parent-inverse matrix to identity, so the parent transform applies and local coordinates land where expected.

EEVEE Next over Cycles: Raytracing with fast global illumination at 2560 x 1440 and 128 samples costs about 12 s per frame, so a 10-camera walkthrough takes about 2 minutes and many render iterations were affordable.

Idempotent, version-defensive look-dev: One pass rebuilds materials, a six-light studio rig, world, colour management and compositor without renaming or deleting objects, and it tests for shader sockets that moved between Blender versions, including the Blender 5.x Glare node rework.
Colour provenance: Brand and cable colours were taken from the project's reference documentation and converted to linear RGB, so the render, the documentation and the physical cabling agree.

subs.name: Render and Export Pipeline
subs.what: A four-stage pipeline from hardware bill of materials to interactive 3D page: procedural geometry from bpy primitives, an idempotent look-development pass, binary glTF export, and delivery as a model-viewer page, an offline zip with a tiny local server, and pre-rendered stills plus 4K videos.
subs.solves: It gives non-specialist reviewers a spatial, physically accurate picture of a proposed installation, including which way a one-way link points.
subs.edge: EEVEE Next at about 12 s per frame keeps look-development iteration interactive where Cycles path tracing would take minutes per frame.
moves: Render lineage: Several full render passes were produced, with low-cost probe renders between them and a final pass that re-rendered only the shots that had changed.
Exposure and callouts: Exposure was raised to lift dark walls, equipment and world, and dozens of debug callouts were kept as hidden layers so the diagram path can restore them.

subs.name: Industrial OT/IT Primer
subs.what: A five-volume, self-contained HTML book (34 chapters) that runs from what a continuous-process plant is, through OT (sensors, tags, PLCs, DCS), IT (firewalls, zones, the industrial DMZ, data diodes), the data path (OPC-UA, time-series stores, ISA-95, a historian asset framework) to the AI stack (local inference, model tiering, the agent loop, a safety override layer). It is the written counterpart to the 3D model.
subs.solves: Process, controls, IT and plant management each hold a veto over an on-site AI deployment but share no vocabulary, so vocabulary gaps stall or weaken security reviews.
subs.edge: It is vendor-neutral and ordered as an argument, unlike vendor whitepapers, standards texts, wikis or slide decks, and it spells out the deliberate boundaries of the deployment so reviewers can see exactly what is in scope.
moves: Sequencing as argument: Volumes run process, OT, security boundary, data path, then AI, so objections are answered in the order they arrive in the room and the security boundary is settled before the data path.

Explicit boundaries as a section type: Named sections state the system's deliberate boundaries (disabled write paths, the role of the industrial DMZ, alternatives considered), and a recurring callout supplies the sentence to say in the meeting.

projects.name: Job-Market Matching Pipeline
projects.tagline: Self-hosted pipeline that harvests ATS postings, scores and verifies them, and compiles tailored applications.
projects.what: Extends an open-source, MIT-licensed job-search framework with a self-hosted, file-based job-market intelligence pipeline. The added layers are ATS harvesters that discover which applicant-tracking system each employer uses and pull live requisitions from those APIs and from aggregators, scorers that join employers to public USCIS petition data and rank each posting against a versioned skill inventory, a verifier that screens out ghost, PERM and staffing listings, and a tailoring engine that compiles a LaTeX resume and cover letter per role. A run ends in a dated folder with a ranked table and one packet per role, and every submission waits for human approval.
projects.solves: Job boards hide what decides whether applying is worth the time: the employer's track record, the posting's real age, and whether it will ever hire, since reposts, staffing fronts and evergreen requisitions look identical to real openings in a JSON feed. Tailoring a resume by hand is too slow to happen at sweep volume. A spreadsheet and manual rewriting offer no filtering and no record of which variant was sent.

versus.incumbents: Application trackers, resume-optimisation services, bulk auto-apply tools and petition lookup sites
versus.edge: Commercial tools track applications, score one resume against one posting, or mass-submit; none joins public petition records to live requisitions or filters ghost postings. Here the ranking function is editable source, there is no per-scan fee, and a human approval gate precedes any submission.

moves: ATS discovery funnel: A staged funnel of candidate slugs, probes, confirmed endpoints and captured board payloads covers seven providers, and each provider has its own hit-confirmation logic because status codes alone give false positives.

Source-split scanners: Split a monolithic scanner into per-source programs with mergeable results, so the slowest source or a board that changes shape no longer gates a run. Bulk probing moved from Node to a PowerShell runspace pool with substring hit detection, because parsing multi-megabyte JSON, not the network, was the bottleneck.

Graded trust, not binary rejection: The legitimacy verifier starts each posting at a neutral trust score that must be earned from certified labour condition application (LCA) evidence, and rejects only on positive evidence, so real roles survive and every drop carries a named reason in an auditable drop graph.

Relevancy with a gap denominator: Relevancy is matched weight over matched plus gap weight, so unmet demands lower the score, which TF-IDF or embedding overlap would not do. Freshness windows were tightened across scorer iterations to concentrate on recent postings.

Resume as a compiler: Twenty feature detectors over the posting drive conditional LaTeX assembly, pdflatex runs at concurrency 6, and the page count is parsed from the compiler log to enforce one page.

subs.name: Job-Board Harvester and ATS Discovery
subs.what: The ingestion tier: Node, PowerShell, Python and bash programs that discover which applicant-tracking system each employer uses, then pull live requisitions from those JSON APIs into a common record of company, title, location, URL and posted date. A durable registry of confirmed endpoints is the output.
subs.solves: No public index maps companies to an ATS and slug, aggregators lag employer boards by hours to days, and several boards expose no posting date at all.
subs.edge: Querying employer endpoints directly is fresher than aggregator feeds, and no direct incumbent covers slug discovery at this scale for an individual. Resilience comes from request pacing and backoff.
moves: Per-provider confirmation: One provider returns 200 for unknown slugs, two return 200 with empty boards, one returns HTML for anything, and one needs a POST against an undiscoverable tenant path, so each provider asserts on response structure rather than status.
Freshness semantics: Relative labels such as Posted Yesterday map to ISO dates with a bounded lookback, and boards with no date rely on a first-seen ledger.

subs.name: Matching and Verification Engine
subs.what: The decision tier: four independent scorers (a company-level track-record prior from public petition data, a posting-level ATS relevancy percentage, an adversarial legitimacy trust score and deterministic rejection rules) plus three-layer exclusion. It emits a ranked, capped, one-per-employer set with a written reason for every acceptance and every drop.
subs.solves: Harvesting yields far more than can be acted on, and three filters (does the employer have a track record, does the posting match, will it ever hire) are not available off the shelf.
subs.edge: Against keyword-match tools and opaque platform match scores, every weight is a literal in source, so the ranking is fully transparent and editable, and the three signals combine into one ranked decision.
moves: Repost and PERM detection: Postings are fingerprinted on an interior slice of text, which survives differing headers and footers across employers, and a single exact salary with repeated identical year requirements flags a PERM advertisement.

Asymmetric deduplication: The applied-company matcher deliberately over-excludes, since a false exclusion skips one job while a false include re-approaches a company, and a shared name normaliser, alias map and short prefix gate link legal names to display names.

subs.name: Resume Tailoring Packet Engine
subs.what: It converts a verified posting into a compiled one-page LaTeX resume, a cover letter and a self-contained packet folder holding the posting text, a structured role record and the exact PDF that would be sent.
subs.solves: Hand tailoring is slow, page overflow and Unicode mojibake quietly hurt ATS parsing, and without provenance nobody can tell which variant was sent.
subs.edge: Resume builders and optimisers work one document at a time and leave editing to the user, while this treats the resume as a program with batch compile, log-verified page count and per-application provenance, and content selection by deterministic regex feature detection.
moves: Fixed-cardinality assembly: A bullet priority cascade fires exactly one variant, so section sizes and page layout stay constant across very different postings, backed by log-parsed page counts and a repair stage for spillover.
ATS Unicode normaliser: It masks style and script blocks, rewrites only text nodes (dashes, smart quotes, ellipses, zero-width characters), and returns a histogram of every substitution.

projects.name: Batch Performance Predictor
projects.tagline: Predicts flux and selectivity from a fiber-spinning recipe before the batch runs, with plain-English reasons.
projects.what: A batch-performance predictor for hollow-fiber separation-module manufacturing. A process engineer enters a fiber-spinning recipe covering raw-material lot properties, solution chemistry, spinning and coagulation conditions and post-treatment settings, and receives expected flux and selectivity with error bands before the batch is committed. When a result is low, a root-cause panel writes a plain-English explanation drawn from a technical document library by a locally hosted language model.
projects.solves: Separation performance depends on factors operators cannot see, mainly incoming raw-material lot properties, and the laboratory result arrives well after the material is spun. The predictor scores a recipe in seconds before it is committed and makes the technical library searchable from inside the workflow. It also draws on the full historical record, folding lot-level statistics from unlabelled batches back in as features.

versus.incumbents: Spin-then-lab-test practice, spreadsheet DOE studies, tuned gradient-boosting models, cloud MLOps platforms
versus.edge: There is no direct commercial incumbent for predicting separation performance from a fiber-spinning recipe. Unlike the spin-then-test loop, it scores every candidate recipe in a single forward pass. Unlike cloud platforms, it runs fully on-premises, so recipes and raw-material data stay inside the network.

moves: Evaluation before tuning: Building an evaluation suite before any tuning reframed the question as whether a batch clears a quality limit, a ranking problem, and surfaced a usable signal that R2 alone had hidden.

Physics-based preprocessing: A handful of transformations chosen on physical grounds improved error materially, lot-aware imputation fills gaps with missingness encoded as a feature, and lot-level statistics from unlabelled batches are merged back as features under an explicit no-target-leakage argument.

Per-fiber TabPFN models: Splitting by fiber type and moving from gradient boosting to TabPFN in-context learning (one forward pass, no hyperparameter search, weights shipped with the model for air-gapped use) cut error substantially, because tree ensembles overfit on very small per-type training sets.

Time-aware validation: Time-stratified cross-validation sits alongside random K-fold, and a drift detector and retraining cadence are documented as design requirements. Learning curves separate targets where more labels would help from targets that need new sensors.

Anomaly-aware retrieval: Drivers are ranked by importance times out-of-range-ness before retrieval from a local Chroma store and a local Ollama model, so the explanation names a specific lot value sitting below its normal band instead of only saying the property matters. The prompt keeps answers grounded in the retrieved excerpts.

projects.name: Multi-Agent Gas Supply-Chain Simulator
projects.tagline: Physics-based simulation of a cryogenic gas supply chain run by nine coordinated agents.
projects.what: A physics-grounded simulation of a merchant industrial gas supply chain covering air separation plants, liquid-product hubs, bulk customers, a trailer and railcar fleet under DOT hours-of-service rules, and take-or-pay, requirements and spot contract types. Nine autonomous agents continuously decide plant load, dispatch, routing, inventory and grid demand response through permissioned MCP tools, shown on a dark HMI-styled Dash dashboard. A parallel shadow simulation runs the same demand through reactive rule-based dispatching so the dashboard can show the difference the agents make.
projects.solves: An air separation unit cannot simply be switched off: it has a minimum turndown and a limited safe ramp rate, product boils off in every tank, and electricity is the dominant variable cost. Customer tanks drain with shift patterns and weather, some stockouts are safety events, and every delivery is a driver bound by hours-of-service limits. Holding plant load, inventory, boil-off, driver hours, energy price and contracts together calls for coordinated decisions that fixed reorder points, FIFO dispatch and reactive response cannot provide.

versus.incumbents: Plant advanced-process-control suites, supply-chain planning suites, plant historians, spreadsheet dispatching
versus.edge: Plant APC products control one plant's internals and need step-test campaigns, and planning suites work at daily-to-weekly granularity without boil-off or turndown physics. Where those tools each cover one layer, this platform closes a single loop across plants, hubs, customers and drivers at sub-hourly steps. Its first-principles plant model needs no plant perturbation.

moves: Depth over breadth: The first version modelled a large set of spreadsheet-driven plants with only a few agents. Narrowing to a small coupled network of plants, hubs and customers and raising model depth by an order of magnitude, with nine agents, is the decision the architecture rests on.

Load coordination: A coordinator keeps the agents from oscillating plant load with four rules: a deadband, a cooldown, a seven-level priority ladder with safety highest, and a direction lock. Approve and reject counts are tracked and unit-tested.

Hand-written numerics: Implemented in pure Python with no NumPy, SciPy or solver dependency. Routing is nearest-neighbour construction followed by 2-opt improvement with hours-of-service feasibility and multi-sourcing, and planning uses CVaR over Monte Carlo scenarios each cycle because the tail of outcomes is what planning must protect against.

Cited physics over a surrogate: A constant-block air-separation model (relative volatilities, a bounded specific-energy figure, efficiency that degrades superlinearly at high load) was chosen over a data-driven surrogate because it extrapolates to trip and startup scenarios.

Physics-engine sidecar: A separate first-principles engine (Peng-Robinson equation of state, MESH column solver) was added as a container, with a drop-in class swap switched on by one environment variable so the local model remains the offline fallback.
proof: 133 Python files, 55,282 LOC excluding the embedded twin
9 agents and 20+ MCP tools with per-agent permission sets

subs.name: Packaged Platform with Physics Engine
subs.what: A package-structured rewrite of the simulator platform (22,490 lines across 11 sub-packages, 11 dashboard tabs, one module per agent) that swaps its built-in plant model for an external first-principles physics engine in a separate container. The engine runs Peng-Robinson thermodynamics and a MESH column solver, with a Three.js 3D plant view embedded in the dashboard.
subs.solves: It raises the fidelity of the plant model and organizes a flat set of about 40 modules into packages, so the plant model can be swapped without touching everything else.
subs.edge: Desktop dynamic process simulators are rigorous but built for interactive use. This engine exposes 52 REST and 3 WebSocket endpoints, so nine agents and a test suite can drive it headless.
moves: One translation layer: A five-module bridge is the only place that converts engine units (kg/s, Pa, MW) into platform units (Nm3/h, bar, kW). Conversion factors are derived from density constants rather than typed, and an eleven-state startup machine is collapsed to the four states agents need.

Graph-based alarm ranking: Nine intelligence modules adapted from open-source social-simulation concepts replaced a cloud graph dependency with a local in-memory knowledge graph, and alarms are ranked by downstream supply impact (weighting critical customers most) rather than severity alone.

projects.name: Pre-Sales Estimation Platform
projects.tagline: Turns an enquiry and a corpus of past proposals into a cited estimate range and a formatted proposal.
projects.what: A two-application platform that turns a corpus of historical proposals and cost workbooks into a pre-sales estimating tool. An enquiry goes in; a low/central/high estimate band, nearest past analogs, a line-item breakdown and a formatted Word proposal come out. One application does retrieval-augmented parametric estimating and the other does statistical estimating on a compact dataset.
projects.solves: The first budgetary figure in a sales process depends on the person: an estimator picks the closest past cost sheet by eye and scales it from memory, so two estimators can quote materially different numbers. The reference data sits in PDFs and spreadsheets with merged cells, broken references and mixed currencies, so nothing is traceable or repeatable. The platform makes that first figure consistent, sourced and repeatable.

versus.incumbents: Spreadsheets with estimator judgement, parametric cost-estimation software, CRM tools, generic AutoML
versus.edge: Top-down analog scaling from historical records answers in seconds at enquiry stage, before a detailed design exists, where bottom-up estimating tools need a converged design and days of work. Every multiplier is recorded per line item, and every output is a range with a categorical confidence and named drivers. Unlike a single-number model, the platform shows which past projects and which line items an estimate comes from.

moves: Small-data ablation: Several model families were compared across dataset configurations and prediction targets. Production settled on a lean real-data set because engineered synthetic rows degraded the tabular foundation model, with ExtraTrees kept as an offline fallback and every compared configuration left runnable.

Two-application split: A Streamlit regression app came first. The retrieval plus parametric app followed because a model fitted on a compact table can predict a total but cannot show which line items make it up or which past project it reasons from.

Audited scaling: Scaling is deterministic, with a separate multiplier recorded per line item and adjustments applied only to the equipment classes they physically affect. It runs in two passes so share-of-total rows anchor on the new equipment subtotal.

Confidence-gated output: A precedence-ladder confidence rating (analog count, cosine distance, extrapolation flags, equipment matches) can set LOW, and at LOW the service withholds the central estimate server-side and returns only the range. Retrieval never pools across commercial scope classes, and a test inspects the generated SQL to pin that rule.

Disposable database: JSON extraction envelopes are the system of record and PostgreSQL is rebuilt from approved envelopes only, so a bad extraction is a data-review problem rather than a migration. A fuzzy linker (rapidfuzz) pairs cost workbooks with proposals and emits suggestions without mutating the extractions.
proof: About 10,900 lines of Python across 93 backend, test and script files

subs.name: Retrieval-Augmented Estimator Service
subs.what: A containerised FastAPI service with a React frontend that retrieves the nearest past proposals within the same commercial scope class and projects a real historical cost sheet onto a new enquiry with deterministic scaling laws. It builds an explicit cost-to-price stack and returns a low/central/high range with a HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence label.
subs.solves: It replaces by-eye scaling of a past cost sheet, which hides escalation error, silent extrapolation, currency drift and mixing of incompatible commercial structures.
subs.edge: Retrieval selects the analog and all arithmetic is deterministic Python with decimal money, unlike a generic document chatbot that averages across incompatible scopes. Every figure traces back to a real historical cost sheet and a recorded multiplier.
moves: Analog-driven ranges: With two or more analogs, the low and high bounds come from re-running the whole parametric chain from the furthest analog, with a fixed symmetric band only for a single analog. The high side widens for each out-of-corpus flag.
Contract-first frontend: A stable result schema let the UI be built against a mock while the backend estimator was developed in parallel, so the real estimator landed with no component changes.

subs.name: Small-Data Estimator and Proposal Generator
subs.what: A multi-page Streamlit app that predicts price and utility-consumption figures for a new enquiry from a compact set of real historical proposals. It explains each prediction with TreeSHAP and a counterfactual lever table, then fills a formatted indicative proposal document with revision-numbered filenames.
subs.solves: It gives sales an explainable, data-backed budgetary number with levers, and removes the retyping of the customer proposal document.
subs.edge: TabPFN in-context inference with engineered physical-prior features was chosen over training tree ensembles on a small table, after a leave-one-out comparison. Every estimate carries a P10-P90 band, so sales sees the plausible range for each output.
moves: Deterministic anomaly rules: Cross-checks on the entered operating parameters are rule-based rather than generated text, because estimators trust deterministic checks more than free-text reasoning.

Live location intelligence: A place name triggers public geocoding and a historical climate lookup whose elevation, dry-bulb temperature and pressure feed the physical model, so a real site changes the prediction instead of applying a flat regional multiplier.

projects.name: CMMS and Construction Data Extraction
projects.tagline: Bulk extraction pipelines that free maintenance and construction records from two enterprise SaaS tools.
projects.what: A data-integration workspace for two enterprise systems: a CMMS holding work orders, assets, preventive-maintenance schedules and labour charges, and a construction-management platform holding submittals and project cost records. It contains authenticated API clients, bulk extraction pipelines that page through full record sets, and flattened CSV outputs for reporting. A public-data facility screening app extends the workspace as a sub-project.
projects.solves: Built-in reports in both tools answer today's question but not multi-year ones, such as completion rate by requestor or labour hours by work-order category, and nested data (approvers, attachments, distribution lists) cannot be pivoted across projects. Managers either skip the question or answer it anecdotally, because the evidence sits in a system nobody can query.

versus.incumbents: Built-in reports of a CMMS and a construction-management platform, manual grid exports into Excel
versus.edge: Direct API extraction with explicit column lists and offset paging until exhaustion produces complete flat tables, and nested arrays are flattened into one wide pivotable table. Multi-year questions that built-in reports cannot answer become ordinary queries over the full extract. The pattern is portable across other CMMS vendors.

moves: Paged extraction: Each extractor posts a table name, column list and offset, advancing by a fixed page size until an empty page returns. This suits an API that caps page size and keeps already accumulated pages recoverable after a mid-run failure.

OAuth client from scratch: The construction-platform client implements the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with a local callback listener and renews access ahead of expiry, so a long extraction runs through to completion.

Nested payload flattening: Workflow approvers, attachments, distribution lists, drawings and per-tenant custom fields are flattened into one rectangular wide table that keeps ball-in-court, days-to-respond and variance semantics.
Reconciling extract versions: Two versions of the submittal extract shape were compared by set difference rather than by row count, to confirm a schema change had not silently dropped records.

subs.name: Facility Opportunity Screening App
subs.what: A containerised multi-page Streamlit app that pulls US EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program facility tables live, computes a gas-flow-based opportunity band for every reporting facility, and plots them on a national map coloured by priority. On demand it generates a business-development dossier per facility using a generative model's grounded search.
subs.solves: It ranks thousands of facilities from several unjoined EPA tables and cuts the manual contact research otherwise spent per site.
subs.edge: Technical qualification (reported gas flow and concentration) comes before contacts, unlike purchased contact lists. On-demand dossiers turn each ranked facility into a grounded research briefing.
moves: Scoring redesign: A contractor-based classification, then a combined contractor and flow tag, were retired for a flow-only model because contractor strings in the EPA data are inconsistent, often blank and often name the equipment maker rather than the project developer.

Safe multi-table merge: The one-to-many gas-collection table is grouped by facility with pipe-joined unique values and overlapping identity columns are dropped first, so merges neither multiply facilities nor create suffix collisions. Missing flow data stays distinct from zero flow.

projects.name: Model Explainability Microservice
projects.tagline: Browser service that shows engineers why a process-quality model scored a record as it did.
projects.what: A small containerised Flask service that makes a gradient-boosted process-quality classifier explainable. It loads a cross-validated ensemble of XGBoost binary classifiers, accepts a CSV upload, computes SHAP values with TreeExplainer across all folds, averages them, and returns a global summary plot and a per-record waterfall plot to a plain HTML page. An engineer picks a record ID from a dropdown and sees which measured features pushed that record toward pass or fail.
projects.solves: A bare score gives operators nothing to act on, and SHAP normally lives in a notebook that most people cannot run. Attributions from a single fold can also differ from another fold, and plots need to use the instrument-level features engineers already read.

versus.incumbents: Vendor black-box quality models, built-in feature importance, surrogate explainers, notebook SHAP
versus.edge: Exact TreeSHAP gives additive, deterministic per-record attribution (contributions sum to the prediction), unlike global-only feature importance or surrogate-based explainers, and it runs from a browser upload with no Python setup. Averaging across every cross-validation fold gives the ensemble's consensus explanation rather than a single split's view.

moves: Cross-fold SHAP averaging: SHAP values and base values are averaged over all cross-validation folds, so the plot shows the ensemble consensus rather than one split's opinion.

Derived time-series features: The model scores summary descriptors of a process cycle (minimum before the ramp, ramp duration, plateau durations, inter-event time statistics) rather than raw tag values, which makes the attribution physically meaningful to operators.

Operational hardening: Models load once at import, matplotlib figures are closed after rendering to prevent a slow memory leak, the CSV delimiter is sniffed automatically, and the last matching row is explained when a record appears more than once.

Portable model files: Models are stored as native XGBoost JSON rather than pickles and dependencies are pinned to exact versions, so a retrained ensemble is a file drop and a library update cannot silently change the plots.
proof: Five-fold ensemble of serialised XGBoost models

projects.name: Scheduled Public-Data Ingestion Flows
projects.tagline: Scheduled Node-RED flows that load US EIA energy price data into PostgreSQL for dashboards.
projects.what: A Node-RED runtime used as a lightweight scheduled ETL engine. It calls the US Energy Information Administration API on a daily cron, parses the JSON response into typed rows, and inserts them into a local PostgreSQL table that an open-source BI tool charts.
projects.solves: Public energy series sit behind paginated JSON APIs and are usually pulled into spreadsheets by hand, refreshed whenever someone remembers, with no history, joins or dashboard. A one-off scheduled script adds another thing to deploy, monitor and forget.

versus.incumbents: Manual spreadsheet downloads, cron scripts, Airflow-class orchestrators, managed ELT
versus.edge: A visible dataflow with debug nodes on every branch and a built-in scheduler replaces an invisible script, with no scheduler service, metadata database or DAG code. Node-RED works here as a lean HTTP-to-SQL engine, needing only the HTTP request and PostgreSQL nodes.

moves: Parameterised inserts: The first transform built one large INSERT by string concatenation with manual quote escaping. The live version emits one message per row with bound parameters, which removes the quoting-failure class and moves type coercion to the database driver. Both versions stay on the canvas so the migration is visible.

Function-node return contract: One-message-per-row fan-out depends on returning the array itself rather than wrapping it, a counter-intuitive Node-RED behaviour documented in a code comment where the next reader would trip.
Warm-start cron: The schedule fires once shortly after the runtime starts and then on its regular cycle, so a restart backfills immediately instead of leaving a gap.

Validation and period handling: Rows with a missing region or non-numeric price or quantity are skipped rather than inserted as nulls, a non-array response raises an error so source schema changes surface, and monthly periods become real dates.
Connectivity probe first: A separate flow runs a trivial SELECT NOW(), isolating database reachability from API-parsing problems while debugging.
proof: Two flows, 12 nodes, and one PostgreSQL connection config

projects.name: Badge Registration Mustering Kiosk
